articles.title: Ethanol blend row: Minister stands firm on claim, demands independent fuel testing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: It was the OMC laboratories’ failure to provide the required result that raised suspicion; the samples were then sent to NABL-accredited and ISO-certified laboratories, says Rizwan Arshad
Minister for Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Rizwan Arshad on Monday said that he stands by the test reports on ethanol blending in petrol that were released by him on November 6.

Addressing the media on Monday, Mr. Arshad said, “We stand by our test reports as the tests were done as per the prescribed procedure in laboratories recognised by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), which is a constituent board of the Quality Council of India (QCI).”

He added, “As an elected government, I was expecting an official response from the Union government, whereas they have made the oil companies respond to us. I have examined their statements on our E20 findings. The OMCs’ release is more about technicalities, but they have failed to answer how much ethanol is in the petrol at our pumps.”

The Minister had on November 6 released the test reports of 63 petrol samples collected from petrol bunks across Karnataka. Of the 63 samples, those from Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) showed ethanol-blending levels of more than 20%, at 31.2%, 30.5% and 24.2%, respectively.
He slammed the oil companies for stating that the samples were not tested as per the prescribed procedure and that the laboratories used for testing were not those specified under the Order.

“The initial 63 samples were first given to the OMCs’ own laboratories at IOCL, BPCL and HPCL for testing. Not one of their test reports stated the ethanol percentage. IS 17021:2018, the standard the OMCs themselves cite, clearly lays down the procedures for testing ethanol content. Yet not a single OMC report gave that figure. It was the OMC laboratories’ failure to provide the required result that raised suspicion. On no grounds can the State’s tests be discredited for this. To protect consumers, the samples were then sent to NABL-accredited and ISO-certified laboratories,” he said.

Highlighting concerns raised by vehicle manufacturers, he said, “On July 28, 2026, the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) wrote to the Union Petroleum Ministry flagging chloride and sulphur in E20 fuel and the damage it was causing to vehicle parts. Within a week, amid pressure from the Centre, the letter was withdrawn. ACKO Insurance told a customer that engine damage from ‘incorrect fuel usage’ would not be covered under insurance. Hyundai, Toyota and other automobile manufacturers wrote in their manuals that using fuel other than E10 would void the warranty.”

The Minister also noted that the report on the same subject by the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) remains hidden from the public. He added that the Attorney General had told the Supreme Court that E20 was still an experiment, but later issued a clarification.
He said the Karnataka government cannot be silenced and will not step back like industry bodies, companies and other individuals who, he claimed, had been silenced or may step back due to pressure.

Mr. Arshad also expressed his disapproval of the Union government’s call for a joint inspection of E20 blending in petrol. He said, “A few months ago, when I wrote to the Union government seeking inspection and testing, they did not respond. Now, when the test reports are out, they are asking for a joint inspection. What is the point of conducting an inspection after setting the system right?”

articles.title: Policeman beaten to death in Theni over Deepavali celebration dispute
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Special Police Sub-Inspector Senthilkumar was killed while questioning a gang who were filming reels about bursting firecrackers on the road on November 8 night.
A Special Sub-Inspector of Police (SSI) was beaten to death by a gang of youths when he questioned them for disrupting traffic at Samadharmapuram in Theni Allinagaram on Deepavali day.

According to the police, SSI Senthilkumar, 55, attached to the office of the Theni Deputy Superintendent of Police, was returning home after duty when he noticed the seven-member gang bursting firecrackers in the middle of the road and making reels on Sunday night.
The SSI, who was wearing civilian clothes, scolded the youths and asked them to burst the firecrackers on the roadside.

As the youths, who were in an inebriated state, did not heed his advice, Senthilkumar began recording their activities on his mobile phone. Angered by this, the youths beat him up, rendering him unconscious.
He was rushed to a private hospital in a police patrol vehicle. As his health deteriorated, he was taken to the Theni Government Medical College hospital, where he was declared ‘brought dead’.
The Theni police had arrested six out of the seven accused, a police officer said.

Special Police Sub-Inspector Senthilkumar was killed while questioning a gang who were filming reels about bursting firecrackers on the road on November 8 night.

A Special Sub-Inspector of Police (SSI) was beaten to death by a gang of youths when he questioned them for disrupting traffic at Samadharmapuram in Theni Allinagaram on Deepavali day.

According to the police, SSI Senthilkumar, 55, attached to the office of the Theni Deputy Superintendent of Police, was returning home after duty when he noticed the seven-member gang bursting firecrackers in the middle of the road and making reels on Sunday night.

The SSI, who was wearing civilian clothes, scolded the youths and asked them to burst the firecrackers on the roadside.

As the youths, who were in an inebriated state, did not heed his advice, Senthilkumar began recording their activities on his mobile phone. Angered by this, the youths beat him up, rendering him unconscious.

He was rushed to a private hospital in a police patrol vehicle. As his health deteriorated, he was taken to the Theni Government Medical College hospital, where he was declared ‘brought dead’.

The Theni police had arrested six out of the seven accused, a police officer said.

articles.title: Trump’s close ties to Nvidia’s Huang scrutinised after foreign intelligence concerns
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Huang is one of Mr. Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley

U.S. President Donald Trump’s close relationship with embattled ‌Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang came under renewed scrutiny on Monday (November 9, 2026), after the company ​said its board was investigating whether the tech executive has been the target ⁠of a foreign intelligence effort.

Mr. Huang is one of Mr. Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates to at least 2025. Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support ‌for the administration’s agenda and become a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market.
Advanced chips are the backbone of ‌the U.S. AI boom and government officials have previously tried to restrict China’s access to ‌them ⁠through export controls to stifle its AI capabilities.

Nvidia’s board launched its probe after ⁠a New York Times report said Mr. Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials believe passed information to the Chinese government. Nvidia shares hit a seven-month low on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. Huang has a direct line to the ​president. A Reuters reporter saw Huang’s full ‌name pop up on Mr. Trump’s phone in December 2025.

Mr. Huang flew with Mr. Trump to China on Air Force One in May, the first visit by a U.S. president to China in nearly a decade. Mr. Huang attended a high-profile state dinner in September for Chinese President ‌Xi Jinping at the White House. The company committed $25 million for Mr. Trump’s planned ​White House ballroom, according to media reports.

The New York Times reported that Mr. Trump was briefed on Mr. Huang’s relationship with the woman and that she was giving information ⁠to the Chinese government, and chose not to act on the information.
Neither the White House nor Nvidia’s communications team immediately responded to a Reuters request for comment on their relationship.

“I’m pushing to investigate ‌Jensen Huang and Nvidia to determine whether our national security was compromised,” said Senator Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, in a post on X. “We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration, who’s making these decisions, and who’s really got their hand on the wheel.”

Mr. Huang’s relationship with Mr. Trump has coincided with several favourable policy developments for the company. In April 2025, the administration backed off plans to restrict exports of certain Nvidia AI chips to China ‌after Mr. Huang attended a dinner at Mr. Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Florida.

articles.title: Hegseth faces expected U.S. House impeachment vote this week
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday, setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power

Pete Hegseth, the U.S. Defence Secretary, calls himself the Secretary of War, part of his effort to rebrand ‌a military he said was too weak and “woke” when he took office last year. Now, with ​a House impeachment vote expected this week, he could soon share something in common with an ⁠actual secretary of war.
William Belknap, who held that title in 1876, became the first, and to date only, civilian leader of the U.S. military to be impeached by Congress.

U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday (November 9, 2026), setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power.

Congressional sources say the resolution may have the simple majority needed to pass the Republican-controlled ‌House before Democrats take over on January 3. Conviction appears unlikely in the Senate, however, where a two-thirds ‌majority ⁠is required and Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats.
House Speaker Mike Johnson opposed the effort, saying impeachment “in ⁠the middle of hostilities abroad” would be “a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see.”

Voter anger over the war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections, intensifying Republican divisions over a conflict that Vice-President J.D. Vance has publicly questioned and Mr. Hegseth has ​defended as “courageous and historic.”

Accused of taking huge kickbacks, ‌Belknap handed President Ulysses Grant his resignation ahead of his scheduled impeachment vote and, according to a Senate history, “burst into tears.” The House impeached him anyway, but the Senate later acquitted him after falling short of the required two-thirds majority.
By contrast, Mr. Hegseth is promising to stay and fight.

Mr. Hegseth has mounted a social media campaign, saying ‌in a defiant video message last week that he would not back down. He also drew a ​comparison to President Donald Trump, who was impeached twice, saying: “It didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me.”

Asked if he had enough Republican support to defeat the impeachment push, Mr. Hegseth ⁠said on Monday (November 9, 2026): “We’re not worried about that.” He announced a Tuesday (November 10, 2026) press conference, his first at the Pentagon since May.

articles.title: Return of patriarch: Farooq steps in as NC old guard reasserts influence to check Omar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In seven decades of the National Conference, the parallel party meeting was seen as a rare implosion and a visible crack that the Opposition parties could exploit to tilt the balance of numbers against the Omar Abdullah government.

The stand-off between the 17 MLAs of the ruling National Conference (NC) and Kashmir’s first political family, the Abdullahs, has had a rare consequence. It has brought the 89-year-old party patriarch, Farooq Abdullah, back into the saddle to steer the party and shape how the government functions, after he had nearly faded from affairs run entirely by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah.

The stalemate began on October 27 with the CM’s Cabinet reshuffle, after which at least three senior party leaders publicly expressed resentment over not being inducted. Later that day, the disgruntled legislators held a meeting, conspicuously in the absence of the Abdullahs, and subsequently submitted a charter of demands to the party leadership, which included intensifying the struggle for the restoration of Statehood and special status, removing Nasir Aslam Wani as the CM’s Adviser and reassigning the Roads and Buildings portfolio, currently held by Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary.

articles.title: Trinamool MLA Paresh Ram Das arrested on charges of rape and extortion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several leaders of the Trinamool Congress have been arrested after the BJP came to power in May 2026, which includes five former Ministers

Mamata All India Trinamool Congress MLA Paresh Ram Das was arrested on Monday (November 9, 2026) from Kolkata’s Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. Police said there were several charges against the Canning Paschim MLA including extortion and rape.

According to police sources, the Special Operations Group (SOG) of Baruipur district police began tracking the MLA after receiving information that he was heading to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. Mr. Das had defeated his nearest rival, BJP candidate from Canning Paschim by a margin of over 40,000 votes.

The team subsequently contacted the Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate, following which the MLA was arrested. Mr. Das is among the handful of MLAs that have remained with former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.

Mamata AITC spokesperson Kunal Ghosh said that as he was with the rebel camp, the police were inactive but when the MLA pledged his alliance to Ms. Banerjee, he was arrested. Recently, the MLA has put a post of social media, stating “Alvida Canning. We will meet again”.

Several leaders of the Trinamool Congress have been arrested after the BJP came to power in May 2026, which includes five former Ministers, including Bishnupur MLA Dilip Mondal. The list of former Ministers who are behind bars includes Sujit Bose, Indranil Sen, Ujjwal Biswas and Udayan Guha.

The Mamata Banerjee loyalists claim that leaders, MLAs and former Ministers who have joined the rebel camp led by Ritabrata Banerjee are being given a reprieve by the police while those still having allegiance to the former Chief Minister are being arrested.

articles.title: Outcry as J&K Bank implements reservation policy pushed by ex-chairman and VHP trustee R.K. Chhibber
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The bank has decided to fill 1400 vacancies, including 323 probationary officers and 1033 posts for banking associates, as per the new reservation policy

The amended reservation policy of the J&K Bank, which was introduced by ex-chairman R.K. Chhibber in 2021-2022, who was later appointed as a Trustee of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), on Monday (November 9, 2026) triggered a political storm with regional political parties, religious and social organisations opposing it, with many terming it “an act of exclusion in the garb of reservation”.

For the first time, the J&K Bank, which provides high-end jobs in a region with a low corporate footprint, is facing a push from the regional parties, including the ruling National Conference (NC). The bank has decided to fill 1400 vacancies, including 323 probationary officers and 1033 posts for banking associates, as per the new reservation policy. It also reduced the age limit from 32 to 30 for the Open Merit and increased the age criteria for the reserved categories to 40 years.

“The existing upper age limit of 30 years needed reconsideration. The recruitment age limit should be raised to 40 years to provide more opportunities to eligible aspirants,” said J&K Education Minister Shamima Firdous.

The J&K Bank is considered one of the main non-government recruitment agencies of the Union Territory (UT). Around 1.40 lakh locals had applied for 1500 banking associates in 2021-2022 during the tenure of Mr. Chhibber, who later faced allegations of regional imbalance with more candidates selected from the Jammu region against the aspirants from the Kashmir division. In spite of being selected as a trustee of the VHP, Mr. Chhibber continued to be on the Board of Directors till 2026 and remained a key proponent for introducing the new reservation policy.

According to the notification, the bank has decided to open positions to 60% for the reserved categories and 40% for the Open Merit. The reservation policy adopted by the bank recruitment included 8% from the Schedule Caste, 20% from the Schedule Tribe, 8% from the Other Backward Classes, 4% from the Actual Line of Control/International Border, 10 % from the Resident of Backward Area (RBA)and 10% from the Economically Weaker Section (EWS).

The J&K Students Association (JKSA) sought intervention of J&K Lieutenant-Governor into the matter. “Only approximately 542 posts fall under Open Merit, while the remaining vacancies are allocated to reserved categories. Merit should remain the cornerstone of recruitment and every eligible candidate must have a fair opportunity to compete. The educated youth of J&K have already endured years of uncertainty and limited employment opportunities. They should not be penalised for circumstances over which they had no control,” reads the letter written by Zubair Reshi, national spokesperson of the JKSA, addressed to the L-G.

The letter demanded that the concerns surrounding the availability of opportunities, equitable representation and the overall recruitment framework “deserve careful examination by the competent authorities”. It pointed out that the bank announcement of fresh recruitment came “after a prolonged gap of nearly six years”.

“The upper age limit has caused widespread disappointment among aspirants. Thousands of young people have invested years of their lives, considerable financial resources and immense effort in preparing for competitive examinations,” it added.

Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) legislator Waheed ur Rehman Parra termed the bank recruitment policy “a concern”. “It’s deeply concerning. The age limit at 20-30 years is completely unfair to thousands of overaged aspirants who have been waiting patiently for years. Applying reservation policies in a commercial institution like J&K Bank undermines meritocracy for our local youth. Revoke reservation in the recruitment. Give our educated youth a fair and equal chance,” said Mr. Parra.

CPI(M) leader has backed the demands of the students. “The government has set the recruitment age at 40 years. Given the rising unemployment in J&K, I request the J&K Bank authorities to reconsider the age criteria and raise the upper age limit, thereby providing an opportunity to more deserving and eligible candidates,” CPI(M) leader M.Y. Tarigami.

articles.title: ED attaches properties in Kashmir in ‘misuse’ of PM Employment Generation Programme scheme case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: An ED spokesman said there was misappropriation of PMEGP Scheme’s loans in criminal conspiracy with the PMEGP borrowers, bank officials of Sumbal Branch and Gamud Gadkhud Branch of J&K Bank and other unknown persons

The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Monday (November 9, 2026) attached the immovable properties worth ₹10.63 crore under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) in alleged misuse of the Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) case.

An ED spokesman said there was misappropriation of PMEGP Scheme’s loans in criminal conspiracy with the PMEGP borrowers, bank officials of Sumbal Branch and Gamud Gadkhud Branch of J&K Bank and other unknown persons.

“The accused have cheated the bank and misappropriated bank funds and caused wrongful loss to the bank and corresponding wrongful gain to themselves. Investigation revealed PMEGP Loans amounts availed by projecting dummy PMEGP borrowers by using fake invoices of non-exist firm/companies and in criminal conspiracy with bank officials branches Sumbal and Gamud Gadkhud of J&K Bank by private persons-cum-brokers,” said the spokesman.
The CBI and J&K’s anti-corruption bureau (ACB) has also registered a case in the matter in June 2026.

The ED said the suspected proceeds derived from the scheduled offences were diverted through bank accounts in multiple transactions and part of it was utilised for construction and renovation of assets and personal enrichment. “Investigation conducted so far, was able to trace the generation of Proceeds of Crime to the tune of Rs. 11.37 crore. Further investigation is under progress,” said the ED.

articles.title: U.K. writer M. John Harrison wins Booker for AI-tinged apocalyptic novel
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: M. John Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize

U.K. author M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday (November 9, 2026) for his enigmatic novel "The End of Everything", which echoes concerns about artificial intelligence in a darkly satirical depiction of post-apocalyptic Britain.
Mr. Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize and a boost in sales and profile for the winner.
Review | ‘The End of Everything’ by M. John Harrison: the aliens are here
A veteran of the British science fiction literary scene, it was Mr. Harrison’s first time being shortlisted for the coveted prize, which critics have said was long overdue.

He beat shortlisted authors Marlon James, Douglas Stuart, Elizabeth Strout, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry, whose entries ranged from a queer epic unfolding in 1980s Kingston to a campus satire set in modern-day London.
"The End of Everything" came out "ahead in terms of both its extraordinary expert writing, but also huge ambition," chair of the judges Mary Beard told a press conference.

Mr. Harrison's 13th novel follows the beachcomber Phillip Tennent and his dementia-stricken, free-spirited aunt Marnie, set in the near-future on the windswept English coast invaded by mysterious objects known as the iGhetti.

An unnamed catastrophe plunges the characters into a murky post-apocalyptic world where the European continent seems to have disappeared and the arrival of the iGhetti, which can imitate humans, evoke interactions with artificial intelligence.
"One main point of the book is that if, or when, such an apocalypse comes it will be incomprehensible," Ms. Beard said, adding the book spoke to the present "moment".
"This is the politics of now seen through the lens of the future," Ms. Beard said in a statement.

articles.title: Kochi Corporation plans water security assessment to strengthen city’s resilience
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The project, which will be implemented with technical support from the Kerala Water Authority, is expected to be completed in six months
A water security assessment project is being planned for the Kochi Corporation to strengthen the city’s water resilience.

The multipronged project, being developed by Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Palakkad, will address issues, including water scarcity and pollution, besides focussing on canal rejuvenation, sewage management, and flood mitigation. The project, which will be implemented with technical support from the Kerala Water Authority (KWA), is expected to be completed in six months.

Once completed, the project is expected to provide a comprehensive framework to guide the planning and implementation of water security projects in the city, said Athira P., associate professor, Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Palakkad.

“Different parts of Kochi face specific issues, be it frequently interrupted water supply, flooding, pollution or an increase in the reporting of water-borne diseases. Water security in a region is assessed based on aspects such as water quality and quantity, water-related disasters and ecological factors. A multidimensional assessment is being planned,” said Ms. Athira.

The findings will be compiled into a dynamic model designed to help administrators, incorporating projections for the coming years. These projections will help identify the interventions required over the next 10 to 15 years, as climate and land-use patterns are expected to change in the city.

“The data will help identify the specific issues affecting different divisions of the Corporation. This will help formulate projects more effectively and identify the interventions required,” said Ms. Athira.
“Such an assessment assumes significance as several parts of the city face challenges such as pollution, water scarcity and saltwater intrusion,” the sources added.

articles.title: Demand grows for alternative greenfield road corridors to Infopark in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: IT professionals flag safety concerns over narrow, potholed roads and traffic snarls, and call for parallel roads through vacant plots to improve connectivity to Infopark

Close on the heels of a decision to widen roads around the collectorate and to convert IMG Junction-Infopark road into a one-way corridor, IT professionals and others have demanded alternative greenfield road corridors to reach Infopark.

Around one lakh IT employees and innumerable others now commute along mostly congested roads to reach the IT hub. Pratidhwani, a welfare organisation of IT professionals that has been spearheading the demand for better road connectivity and public transport to Infopark, highlighted safety concerns arising from narrow, potholed roads and reckless driving by buses in Kochi and its suburbs.
This comes in the wake of a young woman getting killed after a speeding private bus rammed her at a narrow, footpath-less stretch on Infopark road on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

“It is high time the Thrikkakara municipality, Public Works department, Kerala Road Fund Board, traffic police, and other agencies concerned woke up from their slumber, as IT professionals and others have been having a harrowing time over the past decade due to narrow roads and traffic snarls. This is particularly true of the Collectorate Junction-Infopark road and the Pallikkara-Athani road, where traffic congestion is acute. With buildings having come up on either side of these roads, parallel roads should be built through vacant plots. This will help convert many existing roads into one-way corridors. In addition, IMG Junction must be redesigned and a roundabout built, for which minimal land acquisition would be required. Overbridges or flyovers could also be built to bypass bottlenecked junctions,” said Jidheesh Rajan of Pratidhwani.
The aim is to rope in like-minded people and organisations in the matter. Apart from approaching the court, follow-up action would be taken in the form of campaigns, he added.

Sajan John, former chief operating officer of Kochi Water Metro Limited, sought the urgent intervention of government agencies to address traffic congestion and chaos on the 1.50-km-long IMG Junction-Infopark Carnival Junction corridor, which is used by tens of thousands of people daily, including by approximately 1 lakh Infopark employees. Similar is the plight of Kakkanad-Pallikara road and Athani Junction. In both corridors, vast tracts of vacant land are available behind buildings facing the road, and two-lane roads can be built parallel to the existing ones.

Welcoming a proposal to convert roads around the collectorate building as one-way corridors, Mr. John called for a comprehensive traffic re-arrangement plan in the IMG Junction-Signal Junction-Padamugal-NGO Quarters-Olimugal Junction corridor.

articles.title: Trump says FBI looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese agent'
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The sudden emergence of Nvidia CEO Huang's infidelity has created concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence

U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday (November 9, 2026) that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn't think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.
“I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape,” Mr. Trump said at a White House briefing.

The sudden emergence of Mr. Huang's infidelity has rocked the political class and America's tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence.

Mr. Trump suggested the extraordinary step of directly involving himself in a counterintelligence investigation, a sign of his friendly relationship with Mr. Huang and the possible geopolitical stakes.
“I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right, how you're doing," Mr. Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”

Mr. Huang -- a singular figure in the technology landscape and one of the world's wealthiest people -- has acknowledged that he had an affair, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia's website. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing.

“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security,” Mr. Huang said in his letter.
Nvidia announced Sunday (November 8, 2026) it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Mr. Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

The episode is also attracting congressional scrutiny, with top Democrats Sen. Mark Warner and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries saying on Monday (November 9, 2026) that they are interested in investigating it further. Jeffries said the Nvidia issue came up during a closed-door session with the CIA director and the Director of National Intelligence that was primarily about Iran.

“We're going to need a full briefing, specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue, so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened,” he said, “and what the implications are in terms of America's national security.”

articles.title: Dhaka wants Hasina extradited under prisoner exchange
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hasina seeks fresh passport, but Minister Humayun Kabir calls ousted leader a “terrorist” and dismisses request; no response from MEA, sources say denial of passport may complicate matter if India were to extradite Hasina

Hours after a legal team representing deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport for her, the Government of Bangladesh asserted on Monday (November 9, 2026) that Ms. Hasina can return to Bangladesh through an “acceptable prisoner exchange” programme governed by the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty.
Speaking to the media in Dhaka, the country’s Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir described Ms. Hasina as a “terrorist” who had fled to India after committing crimes.

A source in Dhaka told The Hindu that Ms. Hasina has requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through a London-based legal firm, for a new passport and a National Identity Card. The official said the Ministry is verifying the letter and will take a final decision after internal consultations. Ms. Hasina’s passport was revoked soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising toppled her government.

“Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process,” said Mr. Kabir, in response to questions from journalists regarding the request.

He noted that Ms. Hasina is a convict sentenced to death and India should hand over the ousted Prime Minister under the extradition treaty. He added that Ms. Hasina and several of her colleagues from the Awami League are responsible for violent crimes and financial fraud, and need to be brought to justice.

The Ministry of External Affairs is yet to respond to Mr. Kabir’s remarks, but a source familiar with the Indian stance on the matter told The Hindu that the Bangladeshi position of not issuing a passport to Ms. Hasina will further complicate the matter, as a passport will be needed if India were to consider her extradition.

The Bangladeshi official, who spoke to The Hindu , said over the phone, “We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London, seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the contents of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation.”

However, the Press Secretary of the Bangladesh High Commission, Md. Saidur Rahman, said the Bangladesh authorities are “not sure if the request is genuine”. “There is no way for us to verify whether the request was actually made on behalf of Sheikh Hasina, as the email sent by the law firm did not include any authorisation letter or supporting documents proving that the firm was authorised by her to make such a request,” he said.

India had earlier acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests for Ms. Hasina but has not announced any decision on handing her over. The External Affairs Ministry had said the requests are being examined as part of its established processes.
A number of Awami League leaders, who fled to other countries after the uprising, have said on social media that preparations were underway for Ms. Hasina’s return.

articles.title: Why is rural internet connectivity hard to expand? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The past few years have seen a major, but not total, reduction in the lack of internet connectivity in rural areas. Why is it hard to make access more universal?

The story so far: According to data received by The Hindu under the RTI Act, 2005, the number of villages without 4G access in the last four years has declined by three-fourths, a result of a scheme by BSNL to “saturate” all uncovered villages with 4G access. Meanwhile, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has yet to finish procedures to approve any satellite internet provider, which would theoretically bring the number of such villages down to zero.

A major reason why rural internet is so hard to deploy at scale is the nature of that scale itself: villages are relatively sparse and India is yet to be urbanised to the extent of many industrialised countries. As such, telecom operators and internet service providers have to spend enormous amounts of money to reach an exceedingly small number of users. Building fiber out to villages, and then setting up phone towers there, is prohibitively expensive, if operators are only guided in their economics by the number of users that such efforts eventually reach.

articles.title: Mystery of a missing sewage treatment plant tells the tale of the lake in Krishnakanth Park
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Currently restricted to about three acres and divided into three separate ponds with interconnecting canals, the water body is now set to be increased to 12 acres

The lake inside the Krishnakath Park in Yousufguda, Hyderabad, has come a full circle over the past two decades, before the recent announcement by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Development Agency (HYDRAA) revealing plans to develop and restore the lake.

HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath is taking special interest in expansion of the lake by four times its existing size, in order to impound the storm water that inundates Ameerpet and surrounding localities downstream every time it rains.
Currently restricted to about three acres and divided into three separate ponds with interconnecting canals, the water body is now set to be increased to 12 acres.
Work to fell and translocate trees from the park is already underway, with 34 trees marked for felling and 156 for translocation.

This initiative will largely reduce the 22-acre park space and drown its lawns, trees, gazebos and other facilities originally established 22 years ago. The project pivots on the argument that the entire park stands on what was originally a lake.

The lake, in fact, is a textbook example of how governments squander public money with no attention to sustainability or accountability. A simple search for a sewage treatment plant which has disappeared over the years lays bare the whole story.

The Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) was first established way back in 2003-04, with the intention of filling the three ponds constructed as part of the park’s development. The park was launched in 2004, by the then chief minister of the joint state of Andhra Pradesh, N. Chandrababu Naidu.

“There was no lake. Before the park, it was a colossal garbage dump. We got down to the daunting task of clearing all the trash in order to build a beautiful park there. Digging very deep, we built strong gazebos with granite, despite objections that the foundations would be at risk due to enormous amounts of rubble underneath. The three ponds were built so as to provide water for the greenery,” shared N. Chandramohan Reddy, who was then the Director, Urban Forestry, of Hyderabad Municipal Corporation.
Ramaraju, a senior citizen from Kalyan Nagar remembers a huge 22-acre lake at the location which had actually provided water for the crops.

“There was this heavy cascade of water that flowed from the lake through Madhura Nagar, and I remember seeing paddy fields on both sides during 1980s. Eventually with city development, sewage and industrial waste started flowing into the lake, and later it was turned into garbage dump,” Mr. Ramaraju reminisced.

The lake inside the Krishnakath Park in Yousufguda, Hyderabad, has come a full circle over the past two decades, before the recent announcement by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Development Agency (HYDRAA) revealing plans to develop and restore the lake.

HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath is taking special interest in expansion of the lake by four times its existing size, in order to impound the storm water that inundates Ameerpet and surrounding localities downstream every time it rains.

Currently restricted to about three acres and divided into three separate ponds with interconnecting canals, the water body is now set to be increased to 12 acres.

Work to fell and translocate trees from the park is already underway, with 34 trees marked for felling and 156 for translocation.

This initiative will largely reduce the 22-acre park space and drown its lawns, trees, gazebos and other facilities originally established 22 years ago. The project pivots on the argument that the entire park stands on what was originally a lake.

The lake, in fact, is a textbook example of how governments squander public money with no attention to sustainability or accountability. A simple search for a sewage treatment plant which has disappeared over the years lays bare the whole story.

The Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) was first established way back in 2003-04, with the intention of filling the three ponds constructed as part of the park’s development. The park was launched in 2004, by the then chief minister of the joint state of Andhra Pradesh, N. Chandrababu Naidu.

“There was no lake. Before the park, it was a colossal garbage dump. We got down to the daunting task of clearing all the trash in order to build a beautiful park there. Digging very deep, we built strong gazebos with granite, despite objections that the foundations would be at risk due to enormous amounts of rubble underneath. The three ponds were built so as to provide water for the greenery,” shared N. Chandramohan Reddy, who was then the Director, Urban Forestry, of Hyderabad Municipal Corporation.

Ramaraju, a senior citizen from Kalyan Nagar remembers a huge 22-acre lake at the location which had actually provided water for the crops.

“There was this heavy cascade of water that flowed from the lake through Madhura Nagar, and I remember seeing paddy fields on both sides during 1980s. Eventually with city development, sewage and industrial waste started flowing into the lake, and later it was turned into garbage dump,” Mr. Ramaraju reminisced.

articles.title: CSIR-CCMB team identifies potential new targets to fight Tuberculosis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains

A team of scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) has identified critical weaknesses in the bacterium that causes Tuberculosis (TB), a finding that could pave the way for the development of new treatments against one of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases.

The discovery is particularly significant for India, which accounts for nearly a quarter of global TB cases and about a third of drug-resistant infections, according to the World Health Organisation’s Global TB Report 2025 . Drug-resistant TB remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains.

Led by CCMB Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the research team mapped the protein export machinery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the bacterium responsible for TB. The study sheds light on how the pathogen transports proteins within and outside its cells, a process essential for its growth, survival and ability to cause disease.

The research was carried out by joint first authors Priyadarshini Sanyal and Jagadeeshwari Uppada in collaboration with scientists from the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, led by Areejit Samal, and the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Faridabad.

Using a combination of computational modelling and laboratory experiments, the researchers identified 92 key components and nearly 200 molecular reactions involved in the bacterium’s protein transport network. These included the general Sec pathway, the Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system and the specialised ESX secretion systems unique to this group of bacteria.

“Protein secretion acts like a delivery system inside the bacterium and is vital for its survival,” said Dr Uppada. The team focused on two major secretion pathways, SecA1 and Tat, employing CRISPR-based gene-silencing technology to reduce their activity. The results were striking: bacterial growth declined sharply both in laboratory cultures and inside immune cells, demonstrating that both pathways are essential for the pathogen’s survival.

Dr Priyadarshini Sanyal said further analysis revealed that disrupting these systems affected the export of more than 100 proteins in the SecA1 pathway and around 140 proteins linked to the Tat system. Researchers also observed structural damage to the bacterial cell membrane, making it unstable and more permeable. Proteins that normally remain inside the bacterium began leaking into the surrounding environment.

Dr Nandicoori said that these changes highlight the close connection between protein secretion and the maintenance of the bacterial cell envelope, a key factor behind TB’s persistence and resistance to treatment. The findings, published in the peer-reviewed journal Molecular & Cellular Proteomics , could help researchers identify new drug targets, although translating the discovery into effective medicines will require several more years of research.

articles.title: Prashant Kishor’s Brahminical criticism of BJP’s Hindutva
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Jan Suraaj party founder urges Brahmins in Bihar’s Mithila to rethink BJP Hindutva, linking secularism, social justice, and Muslim-OBC political coalitions

Secularism is a modern, constitutional principle. In real-world politics, the manifestation of this principle is tested against a rather narrow yardstick: the fair representation of religious minorities, particularly Muslims. Generally speaking, the English-speaking secularists are unaware of the caste dynamics that come into play in the field operation of representative politics, and they are also resistant to the idea of discussing caste as a determinant.

The intersection of caste representation and religious representation can be framed as an intersection of social justice and secularism in electoral politics. The caste dynamics of politics are often manifested as critiques by non-Brahmins against Brahminism. A Brahmin perspective on these dynamics is rare, and that is the reason why Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor’s address to fellow Brahmins in Bihar ’s Mithila region is an extremely valuable opportunity to peer into the emerging thinking within the community. He said BJP’s Hindu communalism, which excludes Muslims from electoral calculations, has cost the Brahmins heavily and asked them to rethink their position.

articles.title: How AI is reshaping China’s universities

fullParagraphs: AI disruption and a tightening job market are driving a sweeping change across China’s universities; under the government’s ‘guideline on the reform of higher education institutions’, universities will now be tasked with specific goals, pursuing either research, application-oriented objectives, or skills development

In September 2026, China’s government unveiled an ambitious 10-year plan to reform its universities. Driving the change is an increasingly challenging job market for the country’s close to 13 million college graduates, who are facing the twin disruptions of AI and a slowing economy. Under the plan, dozens of graduate programmes are being disbanded, while universities themselves will be categorised and tasked with either pursuing research, applications or skills development.

A combination of factors, some not too dissimilar to the current challenges in India’s own job market, has left policymakers grappling with a tepid job market and a vast number of graduates facing dim job prospects. Top of the list is a mismatch in skills between graduates and what companies are seeking. Depressed economic sentiment has also led companies to cut back on hiring, with the prolonged structural slowdown in the real estate market dragging down growth. AI is the third disruptive force, changing rapidly how the marketplace views and values skills.

articles.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket fridges
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of France’s supermarkets

France on Monday blamed Iran for last month's massive cyberattack on supermarket fridges , summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions against those responsible for the attack.

The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets. In a statement Monday, prosecutors in Paris said they found that Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard was behind the large-scale cyberattack.

The French Foreign Ministry condemned the attack “in the strongest possible terms,” and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, speaking on the sidelines of G7 talks in Paris, said the Iranian ambassador was being summoned to “strongly protest against this extremely serious act.”

“This is an attack of unprecedented scale and aggressiveness,” Mr. Barrot said. “It is the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on French soil, and it represents a major threat to our national interests and the security of the French people. That is why it will not go unanswered.”
“We will impose sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack,” he added, vowing to take “any other measures needed” to respond to it and deter future attacks.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement that a formal judicial investigation was opened Monday into suspected organised cybercrime with the aggravating circumstance of “having been committed to serve the interests of a foreign power — in this case, Iran."

The investigation targets Shahid Kaveh, the leader of an Iranian group described as a “cyber unit” affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, as well as his two deputies and any other individuals who might be identified in connection with the case.

Investigators found that the attackers had used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices located in Iran, Mr. Beccuau said. The Paris prosecutor's office is seeking international arrest warrants, she said.

In the early hours of October 12, attackers remotely took control of refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France. Temperatures reached 50 degrees Celsius for about six hours, forcing stores to discard fresh and frozen goods. The Intermarche supermarket chain reported losses of “tens of millions of euros” in a single day.

The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of France’s supermarkets

France on Monday blamed Iran for last month's massive cyberattack on supermarket fridges , summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions against those responsible for the attack.

The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets. In a statement Monday, prosecutors in Paris said they found that Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard was behind the large-scale cyberattack.

The French Foreign Ministry condemned the attack “in the strongest possible terms,” and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, speaking on the sidelines of G7 talks in Paris, said the Iranian ambassador was being summoned to “strongly protest against this extremely serious act.”

“This is an attack of unprecedented scale and aggressiveness,” Mr. Barrot said. “It is the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on French soil, and it represents a major threat to our national interests and the security of the French people. That is why it will not go unanswered.”

“We will impose sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack,” he added, vowing to take “any other measures needed” to respond to it and deter future attacks.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement that a formal judicial investigation was opened Monday into suspected organised cybercrime with the aggravating circumstance of “having been committed to serve the interests of a foreign power — in this case, Iran."

The investigation targets Shahid Kaveh, the leader of an Iranian group described as a “cyber unit” affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, as well as his two deputies and any other individuals who might be identified in connection with the case.

Investigators found that the attackers had used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices located in Iran, Mr. Beccuau said. The Paris prosecutor's office is seeking international arrest warrants, she said.

In the early hours of October 12, attackers remotely took control of refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France. Temperatures reached 50 degrees Celsius for about six hours, forcing stores to discard fresh and frozen goods. articles.title: Judge sets summer 2028 trial for the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Utah District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028
The man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk will stand trial in the summer of 2028, a Utah judge ruled on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Attorneys for defendant Tyler Robinson, 23, proposed a trial starting in 2029. But District Judge Tony Graf faced pressure from Kirk's family and supporters , including President Donald Trump, to speed up court proceedings that already have lasted more than a year.

Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in the killing of Kirk, 31, as the activist spoke to several thousand people at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 . Robinson could face the death penalty if convicted.

District Judge Graf allocated 105 days for the trial, beginning with jury selection on June 21, 2028. He said the dates balance Robinson's right to prepare his defense with the rights of Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, to a speedy resolution.
Erika Kirk's attorney disagreed with the schedule but said there is no choice but to accept it.

“A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family,” attorney Jeffrey Neiman told the judge. He had argued the trial should start next October.

In a statement after Monday's (November 9, 2026) hearing, the Kirk family characterised District Judge Graf's decision as a “delay” and said, “every additional day without justice prolongs our family's pain.”
Robinson's defense team declined to comment after the hearing.
The defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting. His lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk's death.
Prosecutors had said they could be ready for trial by October 2027. Rather than hold the proceedings during the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, they proposed a January 2028 start date.

An exceptionally strong El Nino is driving weather disruptions around the globe, stoking food security fears and increasing the chances that 2026 will be the second-hottest year on record, experts say.

articles.title: DMK MP Jagathrakshakan, son Sundeep Anand of TVK move Madras High Court over ₹161.12-crore FEMA case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: They have challenged seizure of properties worth ₹45.34 crore in India in connection with a company incorporated in Singapore

DMK Lok Sabha member S. Jagathrakshakan, his son J. Sundeep Anand of the TVK, and his daughter J. Sri Nisha have approached the Madras High Court against the seizure of properties worth ₹45.34 crore by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) for an alleged contravention to the tune of ₹161.12 crore under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) of 1999.

The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan admitted the individual civil appeals filed by the three family members and ordered notice to the ED. The appellants had challenged an order passed by a FEMA appellate tribunal, located in New Delhi, on May 21, 2026, partly confirming a seizure order issued by the central agency.

The issue dates back to the incorporation of Silver Park International Pte. Limited in Singapore on June 15, 2017. The Memorandum of Articles disclosed that Mr. Jagathrakshakan held 70 lakh equity shares, his son Mr. Anand held 20 lakh shares, and another individual named V.T. Thiagarajan had 10 lakh shares with a nominal value of 1 Singapore dollar (SGD) each.

The ED had initiated the inquiry under FEMA after the Member of Parliament disclosed, in his election affidavit, of having been a director of Silver Park International Pte. Limited between June 15, 2017, and September 15, 2018. The initial inquiries revealed that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had no information whatsoever with respect to Silver Park of Singapore.

Hence, the ED summoned the MP, representing the Arakkonam constituency, for inquiry and learnt that he had gifted 45 lakh shares to his wife Anusuya (since dead), 22.50 lakh shares to his daughter, and 2.5 lakh shares to his son on September 15, 2018. Ms. Anusuya, in turn, had transferred all her shares equally to their son and daughter for a consideration of one SGD each on May 2, 2019.

However, all the family members told the ED that they did not obtain RBI permission either for subscribing to the shares, gifting them, or transferring them, since they believed that such permission was required only when the money gets paid, and not before that. The ED rejected their contention and arrived at a conclusion that the family members had contravened Section 4 of FEMA.

The central agency on September 11, 2020, passed an order seizing the family’s immovable properties worth ₹89.17 crore in India for the alleged contravention of ₹161.12 crore under FEMA. Nevertheless, the Commissioner of Customs, in his capacity as the competent authority under FEMA, set aside the seizure order in toto on February 3, 2021.

When the competent authority’s order was taken on appeal to the appellate tribunal, the latter highlighted that the financial statement of Silver Park disclosed that the share capital of the company stood at 1 crore SGD through the issuance of shares.

“Even if the value of 1 SGD per share is regarded as nominal value, it cannot be stated that the shares were of zero value,” the tribunal said and disagreed with the conclusion arrived at by the competent authority that the appellants held no share of any value in Singapore and therefore, the property seizure order was liable to be set aside.

The tribunal had also said: “Without acquisition and holding on to the subscription of shares, the allotees could not have been appointed as Directors of the Company. It is also on record that the subscription of shares was transferred as gift, which in itself demonstrates value inherent in the subscription of shares.”

articles.title: Five injured as bus rams into two cars at Wadala traffic signal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police moved the damaged vehicles to the roadside to restore normal flow of traffic at the junction

Five persons were injured, including one critically, after a bus operated by a private contractor of the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking allegedly lost control and rammed into two cars waiting at a traffic signal near Lodha Junction in Wadala on Monday (November 9, 2026) night.

The accident occurred around 8:30 p.m. near the Bhakti Park signal in New Cuffe Parade when a BEST bus, an Ertiga and a Creta were stationary at the signal. According to preliminary information, another bus approaching from behind collided with the Creta, triggering a chain collision involving both cars and the stationary BEST bus.

According to a BEST incident report, the stationary bus, bearing registration number MH01 CR 3014, was operating on route 6/2 LTD from Colaba Depot towards Gavangaon. The bus that allegedly caused the accident, bearing registration number MH43 CE 1612, was operated by private contractor Chalo.
The impact severely damaged both cars, pushing one of them underneath the rear portion of the stationary BEST bus. Several occupants were trapped inside the damaged vehicles.

Police personnel rushed to the spot after receiving information about the accident and carried out rescue operations. A crane was deployed to remove the damaged vehicles and clear the road for traffic.
According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), five injured persons were admitted to the civic-run Lokmanya Tilak Municipal General Hospital in Sion.
The injured were identified as Shivani Pal (65), Pranish Pal (74), Madhupurn Pal (28), Hasharat Shaikh (34) and Balaji Pandurang Jadhav (35).

According to an update received from the hospital’s Chief Medical Officer at 10:41 p.m., Shivani, Pranish and Madhupurn were in stable condition, while Shaikh was critical. Details regarding Jadhav’s condition were awaited.
A BEST incident report also stated that a pet dog was injured in the accident. Its condition could not be immediately ascertained.

The vehicles involved in the accident were subsequently moved to the roadside to restore traffic flow. Police were ascertaining the circumstances leading to the collision, and necessary legal action was being initiated.

articles.title: Tool developed to test teachers’ knowledge of inclusive education
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nagaland University researchers say the 50-item achievement test is designed to improve teaching practices for children with learning needs
Researchers at Nagaland University have developed and tested a 50-item achievement test to assess trainee and future teachers' understanding of inclusive education.
They said, “The tool is designed to help identify gaps in teachers’ preparation and improve teaching practices for children with learning needs.”

The study by Gyanendra Nath Tiwari, a professor at the university’s Department of Teacher Education, and research scholar Aseto Iralu Meyase was published in the peer-reviewed International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science.
The study said most available tools focus on teachers’ attitudes or confidence. However, few measure what future teachers know about education—its concepts, practices and policies.

“The new test aims to fill that gap. It can help teacher education institutions spot areas where trainee teachers struggle. For example, if many students find it hard to understand policies for children with special needs, educators can adjust their teaching to include more information and real-life examples,” the study said.

The test was built around the B.Ed. Course 10, titled ‘Creating an Inclusive School’, at Nagaland University. It covers five areas: special needs, education policies and provisions, inclusive classroom practices, building support networks and related concepts.
The questions test thinking levels: from simple recall to applying knowledge, analysing situations and evaluating possible solutions.

“We started with 60 questions. We reviewed them before using them on 42 M.Ed. students at our university’s Kohima Campus. We looked at how difficult each question was, how well it could distinguish strong and weak performers and how consistent the test was overall,” Prof. Tiwari said.

“Based on our analysis, we removed 10 questions that did not work well. This left us with a 50-item test. The internal consistency of the test, measured by Cronbach’s alpha, went up from 0.641 to 0.727, which means the test is more reliable now,” Mr. Meyase said.
The results showed that questions asking students to apply or analyse knowledge performed better.

Nagaland University researchers say the 50-item achievement test is designed to improve teaching practices for children with learning needs

Researchers at Nagaland University have developed and tested a 50-item achievement test to assess trainee and future teachers' understanding of inclusive education.

They said, “The tool is designed to help identify gaps in teachers’ preparation and improve teaching practices for children with learning needs.”

The study by Gyanendra Nath Tiwari, a professor at the university’s Department of Teacher Education, and research scholar Aseto Iralu Meyase was published in the peer-reviewed International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science.

The study said most available tools focus on teachers’ attitudes or confidence. However, few measure what future teachers know about education—its concepts, practices and policies.

“The new test aims to fill that gap. It can help teacher education institutions spot areas where trainee teachers struggle. For example, if many students find it hard to understand policies for children with special needs, educators can adjust their teaching to include more information and real-life examples,” the study said.

The test was built around the B.Ed. Course 10, titled ‘Creating an Inclusive School’, at Nagaland University. It covers five areas: special needs, education policies and provisions, inclusive classroom practices, building support networks and related concepts.

The questions test thinking levels: from simple recall to applying knowledge, analysing situations and evaluating possible solutions.

“We started with 60 questions. We reviewed them before using them on 42 M.Ed. students at our university’s Kohima Campus. We looked at how difficult each question was, how well it could distinguish strong and weak performers and how consistent the test was overall,” Prof. Tiwari said.

“Based on our analysis, we removed 10 questions that did not work well. This left us with a 50-item test. The internal consistency of the test, measured by Cronbach’s alpha, went up from 0.641 to 0.727, which means the test is more reliable now,” Mr. Meyase said.

The results showed that questions asking students to apply or analyse knowledge performed better.

articles.title: Social activist Sanjit Bunker Roy dies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre, popularly known as Barefoot College, in Tilonia in 1972

Renowned social activist and Barefoot College founder Sanjit Bunker Roy, who spent more than five decades working for rural development and women's empowerment, died at his home in Tilonia in Rajasthan's Ajmer district on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) morning. He was 81.
Mr. Roy breathed his last in the presence of his wife, noted social activist Aruna Roy, and others close to him, people associated with him said in a statement in Jaipur.

"Bunker Roy passed away peacefully at 6.15 a.m. this morning with Aruna and others around him. He went as he wanted to, in his own home in Tilonia, surrounded by some of the countless people who loved and cared for him deeply and passionately," the statement said.
Activist Nikhil Dey said the funeral will take place in Tilonia at 4 p.m.

Mr. Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre, popularly known as Barefoot College, in Tilonia in 1972. What began in a Rajasthan village went on to become an internationally recognised institution for rural development.
His work was based on the simple belief that villagers, even those without formal education, could acquire technical skills and solve problems in their own communities.

Barefoot College trained rural people in solar energy, water conservation, education, healthcare and livelihood-related activities. Its programmes placed particular importance on involving women in village development.
One of its best-known initiatives trained rural women, including those who had never attended school, to install and maintain solar lighting systems.

The women underwent practical training and returned to their villages to provide electricity to households in remote areas. The programme later expanded beyond India, bringing women from several countries to Tilonia for training.
The institution also worked on rainwater harvesting, rural education, healthcare and traditional crafts.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait

The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: Accused Ecuadorian thief agrees to plead guilty in largest U.S. jewelry heist
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The stolen collection of fine gold, ​diamonds, rubies, emeralds and luxury watches was valued at approximately $100 million, marking the largest U.S. jewelry heist on record, according ⁠to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Los Angeles

An Ecuadorian man has agreed to plead guilty to a federal robbery charge for his ​role in the theft of roughly $100 million worth of jewelry from an armoured truck ‌five years ago in California, considered the largest such heist ​in U.S. history.

Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado, 32, an ⁠Ecuadorean national arrested two years ago in Panama during a layover on a flight from Guatemala to his home country, was one of seven men indicted on ‌charges of robbing a Brink’s truck at a highway rest stop north of Los Angeles on July 11, ‌2022.

The armoured vehicle was robbed while transporting 73 sacks of precious gems and fine jewellery from a major exhibition in the San Francisco Bay Area to a storage facility hundreds of miles south, ahead of another show scheduled in Pasadena.

Mestanza and his co-defendants, who had followed ​the jewellery shipment in multiple vehicles ‌for 300 miles (480 km) while coordinating by cellphone, broke through the locks of the armoured truck while it was parked at a rural Kern County rest stop and got away with 24 bags ‌of treasure, authorities said.

The stolen collection of fine gold, ​diamonds, rubies, emeralds and luxury watches was valued at approximately $100 million, marking the largest U.S. jewelry heist on record, according ⁠to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Los Angeles.

Mestanza signed an agreement last week to plead guilty to a single count of interference with ‌commerce by robbery, a felony punishable by up to 20 years in prison, in return for prosecutors dropping several other charges he faced, according to court documents filed on Monday (November 9, 2026).
He is expected to formally enter his guilty plea at a hearing set for November 19. The 22-page plea deal states he is likely to face immediate deportation ‌once his sentence is served.
In addition to the jewelry heist, Mestanza admitted to taking part ​with his co-defendants in the highway robberies of electronics being shipped by several trucks in March 2022.

Three of ⁠Mestanza’s co-defendants are scheduled for trial in March 2027 in federal court in ⁠Los Angeles, while two others remain at large and a seventh accused member of their gang has been deported, according ‌to the Los Angeles City News Service.
It was not clear from court documents in the case whether any of the stolen ​jewelry from the Brink’s heist was ever recovered.

articles.title: China says 2026 trade surplus surpassed $1 trillion in October
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Exports from the world's second-largest economy have surged in recent months, driven in part by soaring global demand for artificial intelligence-related products including computer chips, data centre servers and networking equipment
China's trade surplus ballooned to more than $1 trillion in October, official data showed on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), reaching the milestone even earlier than last year's record-breaking sum.

Exports from the world's second-largest economy have surged in recent months, driven in part by soaring global demand for artificial intelligence-related products including computer chips, data centre servers and networking equipment.
The trade boom has offered Beijing a key economic lifeline as domestic activity is weighed by longstanding woes in the once-roaring property sector.
The figures come ahead of another high-stakes meeting between President Xi Jinping and U.S. counterpart Donald Trump at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China next week.
Exports jumped 35.2% year-on-year to $412.3 billion last month, according to the General Administration of Customs, while imports expanded 41.6% to $307.1 billion.
The figures brought China's total trade surplus during the first 10 months to a towering $1.04 trillion, according to the GAC.
"Exporters have been the key driving force behind China's economy this year," Zhiwei Zhang, president and chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management, wrote.
"I expect they will continue to perform well in the foreseeable future," he said, adding that he did not think "China's macro policy stance will change significantly for the rest of the year".
The country is well on track to surpass the record $1.2 trillion hit last year, when the $1 trillion mark was reached in November.
However, the export boom has fuelled tensions with several key trading partners, who worry that floods of lower-cost Chinese goods are crowding out local competition.

Exports from the world's second-largest economy have surged in recent months, driven in part by soaring global demand for artificial intelligence-related products including computer chips, data centre servers and networking equipment

China's trade surplus ballooned to more than $1 trillion in October, official data showed on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), reaching the milestone even earlier than last year's record-breaking sum.

Exports from the world's second-largest economy have surged in recent months, driven in part by soaring global demand for artificial intelligence-related products including computer chips, data centre servers and networking equipment.

The trade boom has offered Beijing a key economic lifeline as domestic activity is weighed by longstanding woes in the once-roaring property sector.

The figures come ahead of another high-stakes meeting between President Xi Jinping and U.S. counterpart Donald Trump at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China next week.

Exports jumped 35.2% year-on-year to $412.3 billion last month, according to the General Administration of Customs, while imports expanded 41.6% to $307.1 billion.

The figures brought China's total trade surplus during the first 10 months to a towering $1.04 trillion, according to the GAC.

"Exporters have been the key driving force behind China's economy this year," Zhiwei Zhang, president and chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management, wrote.

"I expect they will continue to perform well in the foreseeable future," he said, adding that he did not think "China's macro policy stance will change significantly for the rest of the year".

The country is well on track to surpass the record $1.2 trillion hit last year, when the $1 trillion mark was reached in November.

However, the export boom has fuelled tensions with several key trading partners, who worry that floods of lower-cost Chinese goods are crowding out local competition.
