articles.title: UFC chief Dana White declines Donald Trump's White House job offer
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Dana White visited the White House on November 9, and Donald Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Mr. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday (November 7) that he had asked Mr. White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding."
The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday (November 9), and Mr. Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.
"So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Mr. Trump said.
"Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," Mr. White replied.
Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody."

The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.

Mr. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" Mr. White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat.
Mr. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.
But there was also some scepticism about the president's announcement, and Mr. Trump said Sunday (November 8) night that he had been joking.

articles.title: Who is Stephen Miller, Trump’s new Chief of Staff?
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

articles.title: FDA adds rare vision-loss warning to popular obesity, diabetes drugs
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss and has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs,

Popular weight loss drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy will carry a new warning about a possible rare side effect that can sometimes lead to permanent vision loss, U.S. health regulators announced Monday, November 9, 2026.

The Food and Drug Administration said the risk will be added to the labelling of all GLP-1 drugs, the blockbuster medications used to treat obesity, diabetes and several other medical conditions. The class includes a dozen injectable or pill-based drugs, including widely used brands like Zepbound and Mounjaro.

The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss. The problem, which has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs, is caused by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve, although the underlying cause isn't understood, the FDA said.
FDA scientists began looking into the problem after the publication of a 2024 medical paper tying the condition to certain patients taking semaglutide, the active drug in Eli Lilly's Ozempic.

An FDA analysis of more than 125 clinical trials found that the problem occurred in roughly 6 of every 100,000 patients who took a GLP-1 for at least one year. The comparable rate for people taking a placebo or other types of glucose-lowering medications was less than 4 per 100,000, the FDA said.
The agency also found reports of the problem in its electronic reporting system for drug injuries and side effects.

Symptoms of the problem include blurred vision, blind spots, distorted colors and other visual disturbances, according to the FDA. Patients experiencing such problems should contact a health care professional immediately, the agency said.

articles.title: How do tokamaks work to make nuclear fusion possible?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A tokamak uses magnetic fields to confine superhot plasma to enable nuclear fusion; despite advances in research, engineering challenges remain, and no tokamak has generated net energy for commercial power

A tokamak is a device that uses magnetic fields to trap very hot plasma inside a ring-shaped vacuum chamber. Plasma, a fourth state of matter, is a gas whose atoms have been stripped of their electrons, leaving free electrons and charged nuclei. The word comes from a Russian acronym describing a toroidal (ring-shaped) chamber with magnetic coils. The best-known fusion energy project in the world, the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), uses this design.

Nuclear energy today comes almost entirely from fission, the controlled chain reaction of uranium atoms, but fusion has always been theoretically possible and a subject of consistent long-term investigation by scientists. When light atomic nuclei such as deuterium and tritium, two isotopes of hydrogen and the best-studied candidates, join, they form helium and a fast neutron. But even this simple merger requires temperatures hotter than the sun’s core, which no earthly material can contain. In physics, this is called the problem of containment. Contact with a wall would also cool the plasma and contaminate it with impurities. Plasma, being made of charged particles, can be steered by magnetic fields, and a tokamak uses that property to hold it away from the walls long enough for fusion to occur.

Plasma, a fourth state of matter, is a gas whose atoms have been stripped of their electrons, leaving free electrons and charged nuclei. The word comes from a Russian acronym describing a toroidal (ring-shaped) chamber with magnetic coils. The best-known fusion energy project in the world, the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER), uses this design.

Nuclear energy today comes almost entirely from fission, the controlled chain reaction of uranium atoms, but fusion has always been theoretically possible and a subject of consistent long-term investigation by scientists. When light atomic nuclei such as deuterium and tritium, two isotopes of hydrogen and the best-studied candidates, join, they form helium and a fast neutron. But even this simple merger requires temperatures hotter than the sun’s core, which no earthly material can contain. In physics, this is called the problem of containment. Contact with a wall would also cool the plasma and contaminate it with impurities. Plasma, being made of charged particles, can be steered by magnetic fields, and a tokamak uses that property to hold it away from the walls long enough for fusion to occur.

articles.title: Keralam cardiologists seek review of order banning re-use of single-use medical devices
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable has become a challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce costs, say doctors

Cardiologists have called for a review of a recent order issued by the Director General of Health Services (DGHS), strictly prohibiting the sterilisation and re-use of single-use devices and disposable surgical items used in critical specialties like cardiology and cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, citing issues of patient safety

At the annual conference of the Cardiological Society of India (CSI), Kerala chapter, here on Sunday, the CSI Kerala Chapter president Asokan P.K. said the association would seek a review of the order by DGHS as the exorbitant cost of medical devices and accessories would make crucial procedures such as angioplasty unaffordable and inaccessible to many.

Prathap Kumar N., organising chairman of the conference, said the rising cost of complex angioplasty, particularly procedures requiring multiple specialised devices, had become a major concern. Reimbursement package rates under government-funded health insurance schemes were often inadequate to cover the actual cost of advanced cardiac interventions.

With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable to ordinary patients was a major challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce treatment costs and extend the benefits of modern cardiac care to a wider section of the population, Dr. Prathap Kumar pointed out

He said cardiologists had sought a review to determine whether selected catheters, guidewires and other equipment could be safely re-processed under scientifically validated protocols and re-used for patients.

“Patient safety must remain paramount. Any proposal for re-use must be supported by scientific evidence, validated sterilisation, functional testing and strict regulatory oversight,” Dr. Prathap Kumar said.

He called for wider consultation among medical specialists, infection-control experts and regulatory authorities to develop an evidence-based policy regarding the sterilisation and re-use of medical devices, balancing affordability with patient safety.

The order by the DGHS said the practice of re-using single-use devices and disposable surgical items was a serious concern from the perspective of patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance and healthcare expenditure. It said such re-use may also expose patients to significant risks, including cross-infection, device malfunction, loss of performance and other procedure-related complications

However, it is a fact that sterilisation and re-use of medical devices, ensuring the integrity of the devices and patient safety, is a common practice in both private and public sector hospitals across the country.

The Cardiological Society of India had in 2017 brought out a consensus document, “Guidance on reuse of cardio-vascular catheters and devices in India”, which clearly endorsed re-use, but set out certain requirements which had to be met for re-use to be safe and effective.

articles.title: NMC cautions students against fake medical colleges, asks them to verify approvals
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in an ongoing case in which the court directed regulatory bodies, including the National Medical Commission, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has cautioned students and parents against enrolling in medical colleges without verifying their statutory recognition and regulatory approvals, warning that fraudulent institutions could be misleading aspirants through advertisements, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers.

In a recent advisory issued in compliance with directions from the Supreme Court, the NMC has urged students to independently verify a medical college’s approval status, permitted student intake, and admission permissions for the relevant academic year before seeking admission or making any payment.

The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida & Ors. , an ongoing case in which the Court directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions. The directions came in the context of a reported instance of a purported fake medical college operating from a farmhouse and claiming to offer various courses.

The Commission has clarified that a medical college’s presence in an official list, or its previous operation, does not automatically establish that it has permission to admit students in subsequent academic years. Candidates must check the approval granted for the particular year and the number of seats sanctioned through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) records.

It has also cautioned students against relying exclusively on prospectuses, websites, advertisements, social media posts or documents such as purported Letters of Permission and approval certificates circulated by institutions or their representatives. Any doubts regarding the authenticity of such documents should be verified directly with the concerned regulatory authority.

For admissions governed by counselling procedures, candidates have been asked to use official channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), wherever applicable, or the competent State and Union Territory counselling authorities. The Commission has also advised students against making admission-related payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries.

Highlighting the importance of distinguishing between regulatory approvals, the NMC said affiliation, registration or recognition granted by one authority for a particular purpose should not be construed as permission from the Commission to conduct an MBBS course. Each statutory requirement must be independently satisfied.

The advisory also asks students and parents to exercise caution when institutions make extraordinary claims about clinical training, hospital facilities and admission opportunities. The existence of a building, office or website, it said, does not establish that an institution is legally authorised to impart medical education.

Suspected fake medical colleges, unauthorised MBBS courses, forged permission letters and fraudulent admission offers can be reported to the NMC through its official communication channels. Complaints may also be made to the State or U.T. medical education departments, relevant regulatory authorities, and local police. Students have been advised to preserve advertisements, payment receipts, correspondence and website details as supporting evidence.

The Commission has separately clarified that courses in pharmacy, nursing, Ayurveda, and allied healthcare programmes fall under different statutory or competent regulatory authorities. Their recognition and approval must be checked with the respective regulators.

articles.title: PM Modi and Railway Minister likely to flag off Bengaluru–Mangaluru–Goa Vande Bharat Express on November 13
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While Narendra Modi flags off the much awaited service from Bengaluru, Ashwini Vaishnaw will do it from Mangaluru Junction

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw are likely to flag off the Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express on November 13 from Bengaluru and Mangaluru Junction simultaneously.

Mr. Modi will be in Bengaluru to dedicate the 7.5 km Namma Metro Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere along the Bannerghatta Road, as announced earlier by Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. During this occasion, the Prime Minister will also remotely flag off the Bengaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express starting from Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal, Bengaluru, sources in the South Western Railway (SWR) told The Hindu .

Mr. Vaishnaw, as promised to Members of Parliament from the coast, would launch the new service from Mangaluru Junction at around 2.30 p.m., sources said. Both the down and up inaugural specials would run simultaneously towards Bengaluru and Mangaluru. Regular services of the VB Express could start within a day or two, sources said adding regular services would operate out of Yeshwantpur; and not SMVTB.

The Railway Minister had, on September 29, announced that the Ministry would introduce Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express as Train No. 26655/656 by extending the existing Mangaluru Central-Madgaon-Mangaluru Central VB Express (Train No. 20646/645). Releasing the timetable of the extended service on October 30, the Ministry had said the services would start at an early convenient date or ‘no booking’ date for Mangaluru-Madgaon-Mangaluru VB.

The Bengaluru-Madgaon VB Express would have 12 halts, excluding the originating and terminating stations. They are, Shravanabelagola, Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road, Kabaka Puttur, Mangaluru Junction, Udupi, Kundapura, Byndoor, Murdeshwar, Gokarna Road and Karwar.

While the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon service leaves Yeshwantpur at 7.35 a.m. to reach Madgaon at 8.55 p.m. taking 12.20 hours except on Wednesdays, the Madgaon-Yeshwantpur service departs Madgaon at 8.20 a.m. to reach Yeshwantpur at 9.15 p.m. taking 13 hours except on Thursdays.
Two rakes required for the service are kept ready, sources added.

While Narendra Modi flags off the much awaited service from Bengaluru, Ashwini Vaishnaw will do it from Mangaluru Junction

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw are likely to flag off the Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express on November 13 from Bengaluru and Mangaluru Junction simultaneously.

Mr. Modi will be in Bengaluru to dedicate the 7.5 km Namma Metro Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere along the Bannerghatta Road, as announced earlier by Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. During this occasion, the Prime Minister will also remotely flag off the Bengaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express starting from Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal, Bengaluru, sources in the South Western Railway (SWR) told The Hindu .

Mr. Vaishnaw, as promised to Members of Parliament from the coast, would launch the new service from Mangaluru Junction at around 2.30 p.m., sources said. Both the down and up inaugural specials would run simultaneously towards Bengaluru and Mangaluru. Regular services of the VB Express could start within a day or two, sources said adding regular services would operate out of Yeshwantpur; and not SMVTB.

The Railway Minister had, on September 29, announced that the Ministry would introduce Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express as Train No. 26655/656 by extending the existing Mangaluru Central-Madgaon-Mangaluru Central VB Express (Train No. 20646/645). Releasing the timetable of the extended service on October 30, the Ministry had said the services would start at an early convenient date or ‘no booking’ date for Mangaluru-Madgaon-Mangaluru VB.

The Bengaluru-Madgaon VB Express would have 12 halts, excluding the originating and terminating stations. They are, Shravanabelagola, Hassan, Sakleshpur, Subrahmanya Road, Kabaka Puttur, Mangaluru Junction, Udupi, Kundapura, Byndoor, Murdeshwar, Gokarna Road and Karwar.

While the Yeshwantpur-Madgaon service leaves Yeshwantpur at 7.35 a.m. to reach Madgaon at 8.55 p.m. taking 12.20 hours except on Wednesdays, the Madgaon-Yeshwantpur service departs Madgaon at 8.20 a.m. to reach Yeshwantpur at 9.15 p.m. taking 13 hours except on Thursdays.

articles.title: NCW receives 1.5 lakh complaints annually, domestic violence tops list: Vijaya Rahatkar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: No woman should feel that she could not approach the NCW simply because she did not know how to file a complaint, Vijaya Rahatkar
The National Commission for Women receives around 1.5 lakh complaints annually, with domestic violence accounting for the highest number of cases, NCW Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has said.

In an interview with PTI , Ms. Rahatkar said there are multiple ways, including the commission's online portal, Management Information System (MIS), email, in person and its 24x7 helpline, for women to approach the NCW to register their complaints.
"We receive around 1.5 lakh complaints annually. If we look at the cases falling under our mandate, domestic violence accounts for the highest number of complaints," she said.
"No woman should feel that she could not approach the NCW simply because she did not know how to file a complaint," she said, referring to the commission's helpline number 14490 and its website.

Ms. Rahatkar also highlighted the commission's outreach initiative, 'Rashtriya Mahila Aayog Aapke Dwar', under which it conducts public hearings in different states to reach women who may find it difficult to approach the NCW.
"We decided that if these women cannot come to us, we will go to them," she said.

She said that since she took charge as NCW Chairperson, the commission has conducted more than 200 in-person public hearings in villages and other locations across the country over the past 1.5 years.

"We have met a large number of women and tried to resolve their problems," she said, adding that the NCW also conducts programmes to create awareness about women's legal rights and build their confidence.
Ms. Rahatkar said the NCW should be seen as "maayka" (maternal home) by women.

"I have always told women and daughters across the country that the National Commission for Women should feel like their maayka -- their maternal home. There should be no fear or hesitation in approaching the commission," she said.

articles.title: Six months into its rule, TVK-led govt. in Tamil Nadu enjoys public goodwill despite concerns on being directionless
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an ‘empty coffer,’ the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures

The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) -led government in Tamil Nadu, which completed six months in office on Monday (November 9, 2026), appears to be largely enjoying the goodwill of people, even though concerns are being raised about the regime’s tendency to be directionless.

Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an “empty coffer,” the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures. The “precarious” financial condition did not come in the way of his government carrying out some other steps such as the extension of the breakfast scheme for school students , the provision of gold rings to babies born at government hospitals, the distribution of eight-gram gold coins and silk saris to eligible women, and the expansion of free travel for women on buses of the State Transport Corporations.

Reports of a “marked reduction“ in corruption regarding government appointments, transfers, and public services have impressed many observers including former Union Minister P. Chidambaram and UN diplomat-turned-political writer R. Kannan.

In an interview with this newspaper a couple of months ago, Mr. Chidambaram stated: “I also understand that sanctions for the appointment of teachers in [government-aided] schools and colleges have been sent by post.”

According to Mr. Kannan, “transparency remains the Vijay administration’s strongest asset.” The ruling party’s national spokesperson, Americai V. Narayanan, says: “He [Mr. Vijay] does not do things to please others or earn applause. He does them because he genuinely believes in them. In politics, where symbolism often outweighs conviction, that distinction matters.”

Notwithstanding the general perception about the government‘s integrity, the two Dravidian majors — the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) — have been unsparing. One of the areas of their attack is on the power front, where the current regime had, ironically, begun with the increase in the quantum of free power to 200 units bimonthly to domestic consumers subject to the overall consumption not exceeding 500 units. The regime’s plans for power purchase on a short-term basis at a higher cost has raised questions about the government’s competence.

DMK president M.K. Stalin and AIADMK’s Amma Peravai secretary R.B. Udhayakumar wondered when Keralam could buy electricity at lower price, why Tamil Nadu has not been able to procure at comparable rates. Besides, even the lower price has triggered a controversy in the neighbouring State.

It is not only on the power front where the government is found on a weak wicket but also on many other policy matters. On the issue of wooing industrial investment , the Opposition’s attack has not been firmly rebutted by the government. As for the TVK regime’s project of building a new Secretariat complex, there has not been any categorical statement from the Chief Minister on the controversy triggered by it, though his Ministerial colleagues, at times, make different observations.

articles.title: ‘John Doe’: Why director Madhumita wanted to move beyond feel-good films
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The filmmaker, whose ‘John Doe’ is set to release this week, reflects on self-doubt and finding her way back to cinema

There was a time in director Madhumita’s life when she felt she didn’t have it in her to succeed in cinema. It happened sometime in 2015, a few weeks after the release of her Moone Moonu Varthai, which did not click at the box office. Disheartened, Madhumita packed her bags and went to Mumbai to join a corporate company, bidding goodbye to directorial dreams.
Even as she worked the corporate ladder, she wrote a village-based slice-of-life story of an old man’s friendship with a young boy.
Titled KD Engira Karuppudurai and released in 2019 , the comedy drama changed her life overnight.
“It was magic. So many people thought that it was my first film; I had to remind them that I had done films before that too,” she laughs.

Offers poured in to make ‘similar films’ — she, in fact, subsequently took up the opportunity to remake the film in Hindi with Abhisekh Bachchan ( Kaalidhar Kaapata ) — but Madhumita wanted to move beyond that comfort zone. “It is a stereotype that women only make good rom-coms and feel-good films. Producers would specifically ask me for such subjects.”

That’s when the script for John Doe, initially titled Sleep Tight , came to mind. articles.title: U.S.-brokered talks are set to start in Abu Dhabi to discuss Ukraine-Russia peace deal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees

The three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States start on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) in the United Arab Emirates, renewing a push for peace after several rounds of negotiations earlier this year.

The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees. U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said on X that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were working on a "negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment.”
Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal to end the full-scale war, now nearing its five-year mark .

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.

Mr. Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects Mr. Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia has not been able to take on the battlefield. Mr. Zelenskyy also rejects any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.

Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.

Russia's chief negotiator is Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who has led Moscow's team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul, Turkey, in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff's operational department Yuri Zhigarlovsky.

Ukraine's delegation is led by Rustem Umerov, head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service, who also attended earlier talks. It also reportedly includes Mr. Zelenskyy's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy Sergiy Kyslytsya and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Mr. Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 10 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 U.S.-brokered talks are set to start in Abu Dhabi to discuss Ukraine-Russia peace deal

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees

The three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States start on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) in the United Arab Emirates, renewing a push for peace after several rounds of negotiations earlier this year.

The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees. U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said on X that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were working on a "negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment.”

Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal to end the full-scale war, now nearing its five-year mark .

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.

Mr. Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects Mr. Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia has not been able to take on the battlefield. Mr. Zelenskyy also rejects any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.

Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.

The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.

Russia's chief negotiator is Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who has led Moscow's team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul, Turkey, in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff's operational department Yuri Zhigarlovsky.

Ukraine's delegation is led by Rustem Umerov, head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service, who also attended earlier talks. It also reportedly includes Mr. Zelenskyy's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy Sergiy Kyslytsya and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Mr. Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party.

It also reportedly includes Mr. Zelenskyy's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy Sergiy Kyslytsya and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Mr. Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party.

articles.title: G7 attention in Paris turns to Ukraine while U.S.-mediated talks get underway in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: It was not immediately clear if the U.S. or any of its G7 partners would announce any new assistance for Ukraine

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his counterparts from the Group of 7 developed democracies are turning their attention toward Ukraine and how to support it in its struggle to defend itself from Russia. As three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States get underway in the United Arab Emirates, top G7 diplomats are meeting on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with Ukraine's foreign minister in France.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha will start his day in Paris in talks with Mr. Rubio before heading to the French Foreign Ministry for a larger group meeting with the entire G7. They will discuss defense and security assistance to Ukraine, which President Donald Trump's administration has reduced, causing consternation not only in Kyiv but in capitals across Europe, the largest of which — Paris, Berlin, Rome and London — are G7 members.
It was not immediately clear if the U.S. or any of its G7 partners would announce any new assistance for Ukraine.

Meanwhile, in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will be meeting Russian and Ukrainian officials in part to persuade Moscow to agree to broader negotiations that would include key European officials on how to end nearly five years of war.

In Paris, Europeans have been clamouring for a seat at the table in Abu Dhabi, but two US officials said Monday that representatives from Britain, Germany, France, NATO and the European Union would not join the main talks but rather discuss potential security guarantees and the long-term security architecture between Russia and Europe beforehand.

Russia has resisted European participation in negotiations and insisted the talks should proceed strictly as a trilateral format involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The three last held talks in February.
But on Monday (November 9) in Paris, German Foreign Minister Johan Wadephul, who met separately with Rubio on the sidelines of the G7, was emphatic that Europe must be included.

“I am still very grateful to the United States of America for making every effort to get the parties to the conflict to the table,” he said. “But I made clear again here that Europe belongs at this table. There can be no solution without Europe, only with Europe.”
Mr. Rubio said the U.S. has no objection to eventual European involvement in the direct talks, but that it wasn't yet time.

“Ultimately, it would be a positive, but we've got a ways to go,” he told reporters after a full day of group and bilateral meetings with G7 counterparts. “But, no, it's good that they're talking, it's good that the trilateral talks are on again. It's better than not having talks.”

articles.title: Bill in U.S. Congress to recognise Deepavali as federal holiday, 19 lawmakers back proposal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: If the Bill is passed by Congress, Deepavali would become the 12th federally recognised holiday in the United States
A group of U.S. lawmakers, led by Grace Meng, on Monday (November 9, 2026) said they will re-introduce a bill in the House of Representatives to recognise Deepavali as a federal holiday.

Ms. Meng, the chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), and 19 U.S. lawmakers, including Raja Krishnamoorthi, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Ro Khanna and Ami Bera, re-introduced the Deepavali Day Act to recognise the festival as a federal holiday.

“My Diwali Day Act will help educate Americans about the importance of this day, and I will continue working to create a more inclusive nation that honours the rich cultural traditions of its people,” Ms. Meng said in a statement.

The draft legislation describes Diwali, also known as Deepavali or the Festival of Lights, as one of the most important holidays of the year for many religious groups including Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists as well as billions in the South Asian, Southeast Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities.

Ms. Meng said while the celebration holds a different significance for these diverse religious, ethnic and cultural groups, the Festival of Lights unites those who observe with reflection, prayer and gathering with loved ones.

“Diwali represents the triumph of good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. At a time when anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate is on the rise, recognising Diwali as a federal holiday sends a powerful message that Hindus, as well as Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists, are valued members of our society,” Ms. Meng said.
Hindu and South Asian communities across the country are facing an alarming rise in hate, intimidation, and targeted violence, a CAPAC statement said.

“This includes vandalism at Hindu places of worship, an attempted mass shooting during Navratri festivities at a Hindu temple in Illinois, and the recent racist disruption of a Diwali celebration in Washington State. CAPAC has been sounding the alarm that these acts of hate must be taken seriously and investigated by federal authorities,” it said.
If the Bill is passed by Congress, Deepavali would become the 12th federally recognised holiday in the United States.
Establishing a federal holiday for Deepavali, and the day off it would provide, would demonstrate that the government values the rich cultures and traditions of its citizens.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth to hold first Pentagon briefing since May amid impeachment threat
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The briefing will be Pete Hegseth’s first since May even as the U.S. military has kept up intermittent operations against the Islamic Republic as well as fatal strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is scheduled to give his first news conference from the Pentagon in six months on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), just a day after a Republican lawmaker launched an effort to impeach him over his handling of the unpopular war against Iran and other actions.

The briefing will be Mr. Hegseth's first since May even as the U.S. military has kept up intermittent operations against the Islamic Republic as well as fatal strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America.

Mr. Hegseth, who has said the news conference would focus on the impeachment threat, is gearing up for a fight, having launched a social media blitz and saying he is ready to defend his and President Donald Trump's actions from “politically motivated people.”

Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican who lost his primary to a Trump-backed opponent, filed the impeachment resolution in the House on Monday (November 9). It sets the stage for a dramatic vote on whether to remove a prominent Trump administration figure following sweeping losses for Republicans in last week's midterm elections that many at least partly blamed on the Iran conflict and its economic impact.

The resolution largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Mr. Hegseth's role in military actions in Yemen against Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela. Massie said Hegseth's actions amount to “high crimes and misdemeanors” and his leadership at the Pentagon “warrants impeachment.”
A vote in the House could come by midweek, putting pressure on Republicans — many of whom blamed their election wipeout on the Iran war — but next steps are highly uncertain.

Mr. Trump has backed Hegseth, pointing to the raid to capture then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January as well as military operations against Iran that he asserts have “obliterated” its navy and air force.

Iran, however, has been able to keep striking U.S. military bases in West Asia and has disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz during the course of the more than 8-month-old conflict, driving up global oil prices. Mr. Trump told reporters on Monday (November 9) that the Iran war “militarily is effectively over" and repeated his often-made claim that Iran “would love to make a deal.”
Mr. Hegseth also has been defending his stewardship of the U.S. military.

“There's a lot of politically motivated people who may have substantial policy disagreements, but their disagreements are with success,” he told reporters on Monday (November 10) after a speech at the Naval War College in Rhode Island. He added that “if we want to litigate” the military actions that the Trump administration has taken, “I'm happy to do it all day long.”

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

fullParagraphs: Meta ‌faces multiple lawsuits over allegations that its platforms harm teens

Meta Platforms said on Monday it would expand its AI age-estimation ​technology globally to move millions more teens on ‌Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if ​they have given birth ⁠dates showing they are adults, as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users.
Teen Accounts, available on Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, include ‌built-in protections that automatically limit who ‌can ⁠contact teens, the content they ⁠see and their time on the apps.
Parents in the US will begin receiving Instagram notifications this month ​explaining how ‌teens are placed in age-appropriate protections, Meta said.
In Australia, Meta has begun using Apple’s age-range signal as an additional method ‌to help determine users’ ages.
Meta said it is continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook ⁠and will begin launching similar technology globally on Threads later this year.
Meta ‌faces multiple lawsuits over allegations that its platforms harm teens.
In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every US state and territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general ‌over the platforms’ harm to teens.
Under ​the settlements, Meta agreed to improve how it identifies teens and children ⁠under 13.

Meta settled with a teen ⁠plaintiff last month in a Los Angeles trial testing claims that Instagram ‌and Facebook were designed to be addictive, causing mental health problems and ​an eating disorder.

Meta Platforms said on Monday it would expand its AI age-estimation ​technology globally to move millions more teens on ‌Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if ​they have given birth ⁠dates showing they are adults, as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users.

Teen Accounts, available on Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, include ‌built-in protections that automatically limit who ‌can ⁠contact teens, the content they ⁠see and their time on the apps.

Parents in the US will begin receiving Instagram notifications this month ​explaining how ‌teens are placed in age-appropriate protections, Meta said.

In Australia, Meta has begun using Apple’s age-range signal as an additional method ‌to help determine users’ ages.

Meta said it is continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook ⁠and will begin launching similar technology globally on Threads later this year.

Meta ‌faces multiple lawsuits over allegations that its platforms harm teens.

In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every US state and territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general ‌over the platforms’ harm to teens.

Under ​the settlements, Meta agreed to improve how it identifies teens and children ⁠under 13.

Meta settled with a teen ⁠plaintiff last month in a Los Angeles trial testing claims that Instagram ‌and Facebook were designed to be addictive, causing mental health problems and ​an eating disorder.

articles.title: Mumbai AQI Rises From 131 to 278 on Diwali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Professor Gufran Baig of NIAS said winds from the sea increased in speed over 48 hours. A change in wind direction took place over 48 hours. The process controlled pollutants in the air

Mumbai’s Air Quality Index rose sharply on Diwali, from 131 in the ‘moderate’ category at 1 p.m. to 278 in the ‘poor’ category by 10 p.m., according to the Central Pollution Control Board dashboard and the Air Quality Index website. The readings covered Bhandup West, Borivali, Govandi, Chembur, Chandivali, Bandra East, BKC, and Bandra West, with Bhandup West recording 276 and Borivali 269.
The 1 p.m. reading of 131 was below the Diwali afternoon figures of 194 in the year before, 181 in 2024 and 149 in 2023, per the dashboard.

Professor Gufran Baig of NIAS said winds from the sea increased in speed over 48 hours. A change in wind direction took place over 48 hours. The process controlled pollutants in the air. He said pollutants from firecrackers would remain in the air after bursting at night and pollution could rise. The prediction came true.

Readings at 10 p.m.: Bhandup West 276; Borivali 269; Govandi 265; Chembur 258; Chandivali 257; Bandra East 242; BKC 242; Bandra West 242. Bhakti Park (Wadala), Charkop, Chandivali, Dahisar East and Gavdevi recorded readings in the 200–300 band. The index places 200–300 in a band above 200.

A court order bans the bursting of firecrackers on roads, streets, and places used by the public. Firecrackers burst from the evening in Mumbai, the eastern suburbs, and the western suburbs. Firecrackers that produce noise and smoke make up a portion of the bursts.

articles.title: Telangana RTC to improve passenger information services, security at 86 bus stations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The transformation plan includes installing CCTV cameras, and providing contact numbers to help passengers access information about Telangana RTC bus services
As many as 86 bus stations of the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) will see improved security and passenger amenities under a project to transform them into model bus stations.

According to the TGSRTC, the initiative was planned after identifying bus stations with a daily footfall of at least 5,000 passengers. The transformation plan includes measures to improve passenger amenities, strengthen the overall management of bus stations and facilitate smoother passenger movement.

As part of the initiative, a dedicated controller was appointed at each of the 86 bus stations. Specific inquiry and contact numbers were allotted to help passengers access information on bus services and schedules. New timetable boards providing clear and updated information on bus operations will also be installed at all these stations.

To improve passenger management and communication, public address systems were put in place to provide regular updates on bus services. In addition to this, CCTV cameras would be installed at the stations to strengthen security and facilitate better monitoring of bus traffic, passenger movement and crowd management through centralised oversight, the corporation said.

“The primary objective of the management is to provide enhanced services to passengers at TGSRTC bus stations, ensure effective crowd management, and offer a safer, more comfortable, and better-organised travel experience,” TGSRTC Managing Director Y Nagi Reddy said. The organisation remains steadfastly committed to continuously improving passenger amenities and further strengthening public transport services across Telangana, TGSRTC stated.

articles.title: Fresh Vande Mataram row in Keralam as Health Minister returns to seat before full rendition ends at State govt event; BJP seeks apology
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: K. Muraleedharan defends his action, saying he ‘will not allow anyone to hijack’ a State government event

Keralam Health Minister K. Muraleedharan returned to his seat before the full rendition of Vande Mataram was completed at an official function in Kasaragod on Monday (November 9, 2026), prompting the BJP to demand an apology. The Minister has defended his action, saying he would not allow anyone to “hijack” a State government event.
The incident took place during the inauguration of a laboratory at Mulleria Family Health Centre, a government facility, in Kasaragod.
Referring to the incident, Mr. Muraleedharan on Tuesday said he would not cooperate with any attempt to “hijack” a State government function and that was what he indicated through his actions.
“I do not need anyone to teach me patriotism. I am the son of a freedom fighter,” the Minister, who is the son of late Congress stalwart and former Keralam Chief Minister K. Karunakaran, said.
He further said he and the government would cooperate with the protocol for Central government events and the policy of local bodies regarding programmes conducted by them.

“If the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation is holding an event, it has its own policy on how to conduct it, and I will abide by that as it is their internal matter. But, if a State government programme is sought to be hijacked, it will not be accepted, and that is what I indicated a day ago,” he told reporters.
The State government’s policy is that only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram will be sung in its programmes.
He further said that a prayer was supposed to be held as per the programme schedule; instead, Vande Mataram was sung. “The State government’s protest was indicated there and then,” he added.
Meanwhile, the BJP reportedly demanded an apology from the Minister for sitting down during the singing of the Vande Mataram.
Visuals aired by news channels showed the District Collector, Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan and MLA K. Mahin, who were seated alongside the Minister, also sitting down before the song ended.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: PRHI denies external pressure, cites ‘a particular issue’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The publisher didn't disclose the contentious issue, citing "agreement and author confidentiality"

Maintaining that there was no external pressure behind its decision not to publish Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Penguin Random House India on Monday (August 31, 2026) said there was an impasse over “a particular issue” during discussions on the "Belonging: A Journey of Love" .
The publisher didn't disclose the contentious issue, citing "agreement and author confidentiality".

The fresh clarification comes amid a controversy over the Indian publication of the Congress leader’s much-anticipated memoir following an announcement by the U.S.-based Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of Penguin Random House, that the book would be released worldwide on November 10.

Several Congress leaders have raised issues of governmental pressure and freedom of expression. Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot alleged that pressure was put on Penguin India to remove sections relating to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS and China's occupation of Indian territory during the PM Modi regime.
In its latest statement, PRHI specifically rejected suggestions that the decision was driven by outside intervention.

“We feel it is important for us to correct certain misrepresentations regarding the forthcoming memoir 'Belonging'. This is a book that we at Penguin Random House India were really keen on publishing as it was a hard-won acquisition,” Pallavi Narayan, spokesperson of PRHI, said in an exclusive statement to PTI .
“Since the content of the book is confidential and under embargo, there was no external pressure whatsoever,” the publisher said.
PRHI said the manuscript had gone through its “normal editorial process”, during which several points were raised and deliberated upon with the author's representatives.
“On some, they agreed to changes and on others, we accepted the author’s position. Unfortunately, and ultimately, an understanding could not be reached on a particular issue,” it said.
The author's team subsequently informed the publisher that they did not wish to proceed with the publication, PRHI said, adding that it respected their decision.

"The Executive Working Group and bilateral cooperation between the United States and India is vital to disrupting transnational drug trafficking networks and preventing the diversion of synthetic drugs and chemical precursors into global markets," ONDCP Director Sara Carter said.

fullParagraphs: AFP journalists heard the blasts, and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an aerial threat

Multiple explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), as the military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
AFP journalists heard the blasts and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an "aerial threat".
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.
A subsequent message from the country's civil defence agency said the danger had passed.
The coalition had earlier said air defences also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.
On Sunday (November 8), the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an "attempted attack".

Images released by Saudi Arabia's press agency on Tuesday (November 10) showed the Riyadh region's deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company's headquarters.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. State Department formally serves notice on India
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Department of State said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case

The U.S. State Department, through a diplomatic note, has formally served notice on the Government of India regarding Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Pannun ’s civil lawsuit over an alleged assassination plot.

The U.S. State Department said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case, adding, “The documents were delivered to the Embassy of India in Washington under cover of the U.S. Department of State note dated October 20, 2026. The diplomatic note was signed on September 30, 2026, and delivered on October 9, 2026.”

The U.S. State Department’s diplomatic note said “I, John Ballard Managing Director of the Directorate of Overseas Citizens Services, in Washington certify that this is a true copy of the United States Department of State diplomatic note signed on September 30, 2026 and delivered to the Embassy of the Republic of India in Washington DC on October 9, 2026.”

On February 16, 2026, Indian citizen Nikhil Gupta had pled “guilty” at a court in New York to charges of murder, conspiracy, and money laundering to assassinate Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The government is yet to comment on the case.

According to investigators in the United States, Mr. Gupta , an Indian businessman, worked with an Indian “government employee” Vikash Yadav, believed to have been associated with India’s external intelligence agency R&AW, to hire a hitman to carry out Mr. Pannun’s murder for a total sum of $100,000. Mr. Yadav, who was arrested in December 2023 in Delhi in a separate case of kidnapping and extortion, has been out on bail since April 2024.

The MEA, responding to Pannun serving Doval, said, “We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials, as also we reject the frivolous lawsuits. Request for serving of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India’s designated central authority, that is the Ministry of Law and Justice.”

articles.title: What are the eight Articles of impeachment filed against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth?
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Representative Thomas Massie, backed by lawmakers including Ro Khanna, has introduced eight Articles of Impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the House; here’s what you should know about them

There is a major shift happening in Capitol Hill following the U.S. midterm elections, as Representative Thomas Massie supported by lawmakers, including Representative Ro Khanna, introduced eight Articles of impeachment against U.S. Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth.
The Articles cite violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela.

Mr. Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend host and one of President Donald Trump’s handpicked appointees in his second term as U.S. President, took charge of the Department of War despite lacking administrative experience commensurate with the post. Despite controversies surrounding his tenure, Mr. Trump has maintained his support and repeatedly dismissed suggestions of dismissing him.
Here is the complete breakdown of the eight Articles of impeachment introduced in the formal House resolution.
Article 1 charges Mr. Hegseth with executing unlawful military orders by launching hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026.

The resolution states that the military strikes violated Section 2(c) of the 1973 War Powers Resolution because Congress had not declared war, provided statutory authorisation or faced any national emergency caused by an attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the U.S.

Article II focuses on Mr. Hegseth’s refusal to comply with Congress’s directive to withdraw U.S. forces from Iran. After both the House and Senate passed House Concurrent Resolution 86 (the first successful passage of such a legislative vehicle by both chambers of Congress in the history of the United States of America) to end unauthorised hostilities in June 2026, Mr. Hegseth allegedly directed the Department of Defence to ignore the resolution and continue with military strikes.

As per Section 5 (b) of the War Powers Resolution, authorised military action must terminate within 60 days (after a report is submitted or is required to be submitted to Congress). Article III alleges Mr. Hegseth continued conducting hostile military operations in Iran beyond the mandatory statutory deadlines of May 1 and June 1, 2026, without congressional extensions.

This Article accuses Mr. Hegseth of “cultivating a warmaking culture” and a “course of conduct that effected the systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defence infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians and non-military objects during military operations”, among other allegations.
It specifically highlights the February 28, 2026, cruise missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Iran, which killed and wounded over 200 civilians, mostly children.

articles.title: Anthropic sends out, then retracts details of IPO filing, emails show
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Anthropic ‌sent out and ​then ⁠retracted details of its blockbuster IPO filing, ‌according to emails to bankers

Details of Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO, ​including plans by the AI company to raise nearly $70 billion, were briefly ⁠circulated to banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters.

A representative of Anthropic sent a copy of a securities filing that showed it aimed to sell about 867 ‌million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 per share, then followed up with an email saying details about the pricing were inaccurate. Anthropic said in ‌the second email it would update the filing later.
Anthropic declined to comment. The email ‌did ⁠not specify to bankers what was erroneous, and Reuters was unable to ⁠determine what was incorrect.

The original email whose details were retracted showed Anthropic planned to sell 866.7 million Class A shares, including a secondary offering. Anthropic itself would sell about 843.3 million shares, while existing shareholders would sell an additional ​23.3 million shares. The IPO would ‌raise $69.3 billion at the top of the range.

Separately, the original filing showed that Anthropic had lined up $26 billion in investments from some of the world’s biggest technology companies alongside its IPO, underscoring the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom.

Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, ‌Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC had agreed to participate in the ​private placement of Anthropic’s Class N common stock at the IPO price, which would close immediately after the IPO, the original filing showed.
Anthropic is ⁠expected to formally launch the roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected in the following week.

The Anthropic IPO comes at a time when other companies in the AI infrastructure and data center ‌sectors have delayed or withdrawn their planned listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave Inc and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, but expectations have since come down, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end of the range, Reuters previously reported.

Founded in ‌2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic’s president, Anthropic ​has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models.

Anthropic ‌sent out and ​then ⁠retracted details of its blockbuster IPO filing, ‌according to emails to bankers

Details of Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO, ​including plans by the AI company to raise nearly $70 billion, were briefly ⁠circulated to banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters.

A representative of Anthropic sent a copy of a securities filing that showed it aimed to sell about 867 ‌million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 per share, then followed up with an email saying details about the pricing were inaccurate. Anthropic said in ‌the second email it would update the filing later.

Anthropic declined to comment. The email ‌did ⁠not specify to bankers what was erroneous, and Reuters was unable to ⁠determine what was incorrect.

The original email whose details were retracted showed Anthropic planned to sell 866.7 million Class A shares, including a secondary offering. Anthropic itself would sell about 843.3 million shares, while existing shareholders would sell an additional ​23.3 million shares. The IPO would ‌raise $69.3 billion at the top of the range.

Separately, the original filing showed that Anthropic had lined up $26 billion in investments from some of the world’s biggest technology companies alongside its IPO, underscoring the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom.

Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, ‌Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC had agreed to participate in the ​private placement of Anthropic’s Class N common stock at the IPO price, which would close immediately after the IPO, the original filing showed.

Anthropic is ⁠expected to formally launch the roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected in the following week.

The Anthropic IPO comes at a time when other companies in the AI infrastructure and data center ‌sectors have delayed or withdrawn their planned listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave Inc and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, but expectations have since come down, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end of the range, Reuters previously reported.

Founded in ‌2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic’s president, Anthropic ​has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models.

articles.title: 331 tonnes of garbage removed from Madurai city after Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Madurai Corporation cleared a total of 331 tonnes of garbage, till 6 p.m. on Monday, which was generated across the city on Deepavali day.
Along with the corporation cleanliness workers, volunteers from the Democratic Youth Federation of India, joined the mass cleaning drive early on Monday morning.
Mayor (in-charge), T. Nagarajan, and Corporation Commissioner, Gaurav Kumar, inaugurated the cleanliness drive.

The drive started on the Chithrai Streets, Aavani Moola Streets, Masi Streets, Veli Streets and Vilakkuthoon junction around Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple where commercial establishments, especially textile showrooms, are located.
Besides, the workers focussed on spots at Teppakulam, Mattuthavani bus stand and Vaigai Bank Roads where garbage accumulation is higher.
Besides the usual vehicles used for transporting garbage, 11 earth movers, five bobcat machinery, nine tipper trucks and 42 tractors were involved in the exercise.

The work was expedited in the early hours so much so that 128.40 tonnes of garbage was cleared in the city by 12 noon. This was 33.32 tonnes of additional festival-time garbage removed when compared to 95.08 tonnes cleared during the same time in the last Deepavali season.
The workers had already removed 137 tonnes of garbage on Deepavali day (Sunday).
City Health Officer, Aravind Jothi, Assistant Health Officer, Abishek, DYFI district president, Selva, and secretary, Vel Deva, were present.

articles.title: Keralam CPI(M) awaits ICC report on complaint against former Palakkad secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Complainant had made allegations of sexual misconduct against Babu; party State leadership to decide on further action based on findings in report

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has stepped up its internal inquiry into a sexual misconduct complaint against former Palakkad district secretary E.N. Suresh Babu. The party’s internal complaints committee (ICC) is investigating the complaint. It has reportedly completed key procedures, including recording the statement of the woman who filed the complaint.
The complainant is a lawyer and a party leader. She is understood to have submitted digital evidence in support of her allegations against Mr. Babu.

The ICC will submit its inquiry report and recommendations to the CPI(M) State committee after completing the investigation. The State leadership will decide on further action against Mr. Babu based on the findings. The possibility of disciplinary action, including removal from primary membership, is also being discussed within the party.

As per the party’s rules, a complaint against a leader of an organisational unit must be investigated by the ICC of the next higher committee. Since Mr. Babu was the Palakkad district secretary when the complaint was raised, the matter was referred to the ICC under the party central committee.

The woman’s complaint had earlier led to the intervention of the State leadership and Mr. Babu’s removal from the district secretary post. On October 4, the party appointed former MLA V. Chenthamarakshan as his successor at an extended district committee meeting. The CPI(M) had officially described the change as part of its organisational review following the electoral setback.

The party had maintained that Mr. Babu stepped down voluntarily due to personal reasons, denying any link between his removal and the complaint. However, the ICC inquiry has brought the circumstances surrounding his exit as district secretary back into focus.
The complaint reportedly relates to an incident at the CPI(M) district committee office in Palakkad, where the woman had been called.

The issue is likely to come up for further discussion at the State leadership level after the ICC submits its report. The findings and recommendations will determine the next course of action against Mr. Babu.

articles.title: Delhi Police Crime Branch registers FIR over fake notices seeking blocking of IFF, SFLC X accounts; probes ‘imposter’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: X had told the Delhi High Court that the takedown requests purportedly issued in the name of the Delhi Police were fraudulent; the force’s IFSO unit will assist in the investigation

The Delhi Police’s Crime Branch has registered a case over fraudulent notices purportedly issued in the name of the force, seeking the removal of social media posts and the blocking of accounts belonging to the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and the Software Freedom Law Centre (SFLC), an official close to the development told The Hindu.
The FIR has been registered on charges of impersonating a public servant and forgery under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Section 66 of Information Technology (IT) Act.

The development comes days after social media platform X told the Delhi High Court that an internal investigation had established that the notices were not genuine police communications and had been sent by an “imposter”. The platform also told the court that it had not acted on the requests and would not take down the organisations’ accounts.

The case follows a November 6 hearing before Justice Amit Mahajan, who was hearing petitions filed by the two digital rights organisations challenging the purported takedown requests. X’s counsel told the court that the platform had conducted an internal investigation and found that someone had impersonated the Delhi Police.
“We did not act on it. Notices are not sent by the Delhi Police. We have filed a complaint with the Delhi Police last night to find the imposter,” X’s counsel submitted.
The court recorded the platform’s assurance and disposed of the petitions, granting the organisations liberty to approach it again if any action was taken against their accounts.

The controversy began after X forwarded two purported ‘Illegal Content Reports’ to IFF on November 3. The first, dated October 31, sought the removal of a post published by IFF on October 30 and another post by SFLC. The second, dated November 2, sought the removal of 37 posts and the blocking of three accounts — @internetfreedom, @SFLCin and @geoblockedindia — in their entirety.

The notices alleged that the posts were “defamatory” towards the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). They reportedly called for the content to be removed or withheld within three hours, citing provisions of the Information Technology Act and the IT Rules, 2021.

IFF had said that the posts in question reproduced and commented on a legal notice purportedly sent to the organisation on behalf of the RSS. It maintained that the posts constituted protected speech under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution and that it had not been given prior notice before the takedown requests were submitted.
The organisation subsequently served a legal notice on the Delhi Police and X Corp. through its counsel, seeking clarification over the requests.
