articles.title: Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s bail plea dismissed in alleged multi-crore private school bribery case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Anbil Mahesh was arrested on October 26 and remanded in judicial custody till November 18

A special court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the bail petition filed by former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, who is accused of receiving a share of an alleged multi-crore bribe collected from private school managements allegedly through threats, deception, and false promises of securing government approvals.

D.C. Elangovan, secretary of the Private School Management Association, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Commissioner of Police on June 23, 2026, alleging that nearly ₹100 crore had been collected from private school managements through intimidation and forgery.

The complaint named B.T. Arasakumar (Accused 1), who allegedly floated an unregistered body called the Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association (TNPSA), claiming to be its founder-president, and Muthukumar (Accused 2), a former MLA from Virudhachalam, as the key persons involved in the collection of bribes.

The two allegedly organised an event of the TNPSA at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024, which Mr. Poyyamozhi attended as the chief guest. The prosecution alleged that a bank account was subsequently opened in the name of BTK Educational Development Trust at the Canara Bank’s Tondiarpet branch; this account was used to collect membership fees and other amounts from private schools.

The FIR alleged that the accused assured school managements that they could obtain government approvals and permissions easily, even if their institutions lacked basic requirements. They allegedly threatened that schools refusing to pay the demanded amounts would not receive the necessary permissions, potentially affecting students appearing for the SSLC and Class XII public examinations.

Dismissing the bail petition, Special Court Judge L.S. Sathiyamurthy noted that statements from witnesses, including private school correspondents and managers, had been recorded by the investigating officer and before the Judicial Magistrate. “A preliminary examination of these statements indicated a prima facie link between the petitioner and the alleged offence,” the judge observed.

The investigating agency had also seized computers and other digital devices from Mr. Poyyamozhi’s premises and sent them to a forensic laboratory for examination. The court said it would have to await the findings of the cyber forensic experts.

D.C. Elangovan, secretary of the Private School Management Association, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Commissioner of Police on June 23, 2026, alleging that nearly ₹100 crore had been collected from private school managements through intimidation and forgery.

The two allegedly organised an event of the TNPSA at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024, which Mr. Poyyamozhi attended as the chief guest. The prosecution alleged that a bank account was subsequently opened in the name of BTK Educational Development Trust at the Canara Bank’s Tondiarpet branch; this account was used to collect membership fees and other amounts from private schools.

The FIR alleged that the accused assured school managements that they could obtain government approvals and permissions easily, even if their institutions lacked basic requirements. Observing that the investigation was still at an early stage and the first period of remand had only just concluded, the Special Court Judge said the materials collected so far indicated that substantial sums had been extorted from multiple private school managements through deception and threats. Witness statements suggested that money collected by A1, A2, and their associates had reached the petitioner under the guise of a ‘party fund’, it said.

Classifying the case as a multi-crore economic offence involving several victims, the court pointed out that some of the accused were yet to be arrested and the custodial interrogation of Muthukumar who had surrendered after the arrest of Mr. Poyyamozhi and other accused, was at an initial stage.

articles.title: Poland arrests two Ukrainians over alleged Russian espionage, sabotage

fullParagraphs: Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine
Poland has arrested two Ukrainian men suspected of espionage ​and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence ‌services, the Internal Security Agency (ABW) ​said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia has repeatedly ‌denied the accusations.

“According to findings ‌by ⁠the ABW, the suspects carried ⁠out tasks on behalf of Russian special services, which included, among other things, reconnoitring critical infrastructure ​and military facilities ‌throughout the country,” the agency said in a statement.

“The prosecutor has charged both detainees with engaging in espionage activities ‌on behalf of a foreign ​intelligence service against the Republic of Poland, as well as ⁠committing acts of sabotage.”

According to investigators, the men set fire to vehicles after replacing ‌their licence plates with ones resembling those used by the Ukrainian military. The men were paid for carrying out the tasks, including in cryptocurrencies.

“The investigation has established that the ‌acts of sabotage were carried out at the ​behest of Russian intelligence services and were intended to fuel anti-Ukrainian ⁠sentiment,” prosecutors said in a separate statement.
Both ⁠face from 10 years to life imprisonment if found guilty.
The Russian ‌embassy in Warsaw did not immediately respond to an emailed request ​for comment.

articles.title: U.S. judge orders psychiatric exam for Meghan Markle's father
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Thomas Markle, 82, is charged with one count of "possession of child pornography" and made an initial court appearance in Tampa, Florida

A U.S. judge has ordered a psychiatric examination for Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Prince Harry's wife, Meghan Markle, after his arrest for alleged possession of images of child sexual abuse.
Thomas Markle, 82, is charged with one count of "possession of child pornography" and made an initial court appearance in Tampa in Florida on Friday (November 6, 2026).
Judge Lindsay Griffin cited his "health condition," "advanced age" and "lack of recall" in the order issued without providing further details.
Thomas Markle was taken into custody by FBI agents earlier that day at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida.

The Justice Department said he allegedly "kept child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades."
Pictures of child sex abuse have also allegedly been found at Thomas Markle's former home in the Philippines and at a storage unit he rented in Mexico.

The judge said she found "reasonable cause to believe" that Thomas Markle was suffering from a condition "rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense."
She instructed a psychiatrist to provide a report on Markle's mental state by November 20.
The judge permitted Markle to be moved to house arrest with electronic monitoring, CNN reported.
Markle had been living in Cebu in the Philippines until reportedly returning to the United States this year.

articles.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh: Sources
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: AFP journalists heard the blasts, and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an aerial threat

Multiple explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), as the military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
AFP journalists heard the blasts and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an "aerial threat".
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.
A subsequent message from the country's civil defence agency said the danger had passed.
The coalition had earlier said air defences also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.
On Sunday (November 8), the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an "attempted attack".

Images released by Saudi Arabia's press agency on Tuesday (November 10) showed the Riyadh region's deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company's headquarters.

"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.

A subsequent message from the country's civil defence agency said the danger had passed.

The coalition had earlier said air defences also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.

Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.

On Sunday (November 8), the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.

Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an "attempted attack".

Images released by Saudi Arabia's press agency on Tuesday (November 10) showed the Riyadh region's deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company's headquarters.

articles.title: Kadambini Ganguly: breaking barriers in medicine
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: In her time, Kadambini Ganguly challenged convention to become the first Indian female doctor to practice Western medicine

Have you heard of the names Kadambini Ganguly and Anandibai Joshi? Considered India’s first female doctors, these names have often been looked past in the pages of history and even medical textbooks. Today, let’s talk about the story of Kadambini Ganguly — India’s first practising lady doctor.

It was in 1861 that Brahmo reformer and headmaster Braja Kishore Basu had a daughter. She was named Kadambini Basu. Young Kadambini, despite hailing from a community that did not necessarily support women’s education like many others at the time did, received an education at the Brahmo Eden Female School and later at the Hindu Mahila Vidyalaya.

As the daughter of someone who organised and fought for women’s emancipation, Kadambini went on to study in college and became the first woman to pass the University of Calcutta entrance examination. In 1882, she passed the examination for the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree along with Chandramukhi Basu from the University of Calcutta, making her and Chandramukhi the first female graduates in the country.

Wanting to study medicine, Kadambini decided to enrol at the Calcutta Medical College after graduation. She was, however, believed to have been unable to receive the BMC certificate due to a shortage of a couple of marks. She did receive the GBMC (Graduate of Bengal Medical College) degree, though, in 1886. Thus, she became the first Indian woman to be allowed to practice Western medicine.

Around 1888, Kadambini started working at the Lady Dufferin Hospital for a monthly salary of 300 rupees. She had even gone to Nepal to treat British royalty. Along with pursuing medicine, she was also politically quite vocal and active. Around 1899, Kadambini was one of the first women delegates elected to the Fifth Session of the Congress in Bombay and the next year, she won to become the first women speaker at the Congress.

She also served as the president of the Transvaal Indian Association, founded by Gandhiji’s colleague Henry Pollock. She was a member of the Women’s Conference held in Calcutta and even presided over the General Brahmo Samaj session in Calcutta.

Around 1883, Kadambini married Dwarakanath Ganguly (thus the change in name from Kadambini Bose to Kadambini Ganguly in many documents). Dwarakanath Ganguly was a Bengali Brahmo reformer, educator, journalist, and pioneer of women’s rights in British India.

She was a mother to eight children and is often said to have been deft in needlework. She became a practising doctor while equally devoting herself to family and household affairs, an action which was deemed impossible by many in the era.

Despite having being burdened with domestic chores, like most women of that time, Kadambini still managed to smash the glass ceilings and societal stereotypes in both her professional and personal life.
A name which should not be forgotten in the course of time, Dr Kadambini is a reason many of us are able to pursue our passion — in medicine and in life.

articles.title: Health department to probe allegations of medical negligence at North Paravur Government Taluk Hospital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The regional Vigilance unit of the Health department will probe allegations of medical negligence in the treatment of a 56-year-old native of Kunnukara at the Government Taluk Hospital in North Paravur, Ernakulam.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan had directed the authorities to conduct an inquiry into the charge that the right leg of the patient, Abdul Jabbar, had to be amputated below the knee following delayed diagnosis and treatment.

The medical superintendent had submitted a preliminary report to the District Medical Officer denying charges of medical negligence. The surgeon had referred the patient to the Government Medical College Hospital, Kottayam, but the patient reportedly refused to comply with the instructions and sought discharge against medical advice. This was recorded in the hospital register, according to the authorities.

Mr. Jabbar told the media that he had sought treatment at the emergency wing of the hospital on July 26, 2026, after experiencing intense pain in his right foot. He alleged that the duty doctors treated the symptoms with painkillers without realising that the underlying cause was a stroke blocking blood flow to the leg. He alleged that his condition worsened after he returned the next day to consult the surgeon.

Meanwhile, North Paravur municipal chairperson Ramesh D. Kurup accused the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] of trying to politicise the issue. He said action would be taken against the hospital staff, if required, based on the findings of the probe.

Activists of the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) took out a march to the hospital on Tuesday (November 10), alleging medical negligence. They demanded that the government provide compensation to the patient.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

articles.title: Singareni plans to increase coal supplies to TG-Genco to 75K tonnes a day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Priority will be given to TG-Genco in Naini coal supply over Gencos of AP, Maha, K’taka, TN: SCCL CMD Buddhaprakash Jyoti

With the demand for energy expected to rise further in the coming days due to the impact of El Nino conditions, the Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) has decided to supply 75,000 tonnes of coal per day to the thermal power projects of the Telangana Power Generation Corporation Ltd (TG-Genco).

It includes supply of at least 16,000 tonnes of coal every day from the Naini coal mine in Odisha to the Yadadri Thermal Power Station (YTPS) and arrangements are being made to transport it seamlessly. The decisions were taken at a high-level coordination meeting held virtually at Singareni Bhavan, the corporate office of SCCL, here on Tuesday.

Chairman and Managing Director of SCCL Buddhaprakash Jyoti and CMD of Telangana Genco CMD S. Harish chaired the meeting from their offices. Coordination meetings are being held between SCCL and Genco on coal supplies to the latter’s thermal power plants. At the Tuesday’s meeting, it was decided to further increase the coal supplied further to Telangana Genco.

The Singareni CMD instructed the company’s Directors and area General Managers to give first priority to coal transportation to Genco’s thermal power plants and to supply coal to other States’ power plants only after meeting Telangana Genco’s requirements.

He stated that the Telangana Genco had been getting higher coal supplies from Singareni this year, compared to the past three to four years. Singareni was ready to supply additional coal to the extent of its capacity, if the State’s energy requirements increase.

Stating that the Naini mine had set a target of producing around 20,000 tonnes of coal per day and currently it was holding a stock of 3,00,000 tonnes, Mr. Buddhaprakash Jyoti urged the Genco to take steps to step up coal transport to YTPS. Mr. Harish explained that local transportation issues had caused some delays and that plans were in place to transport 16,000 tonnes per day from the end of this month.

The Genco CMD said measures were being taken to improve coal transportation by road from the mine to the nearest railway siding. He expressed satisfaction that coal transportation had increased following the coordination meetings.

The Naini General Manager noted that several private companies in the region, as well as the Gencos of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu had sought Naini coal. The Singareni CMD instructed the Marketing Department officials to give Telangana Genco first priority for coal produced at Naini and to make arrangements to transport the remaining coal to meet the requirements of other Gencos.

articles.title: Passenger jumps onto track at Vijayanagar Metro station; Purple Line services briefly disrupted
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), the incident occurred at approximately 1.31 p.m.

Bengaluru Metro services on the Purple Line were briefly disrupted on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) after a passenger jumped onto the track at Vijayanagar Metro Station while a train was approaching the platform.

According to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), the incident occurred at approximately 1.31 p.m. Station authorities immediately initiated emergency protocols, rescued the individual and shifted the passenger to a nearby hospital for medical treatment.

To facilitate rescue and safety operations while minimising inconvenience to commuters, BMRCL operated truncated services on two unaffected sections of the Purple Line — between Kempegowda (Majestic) and Whitefield (Kadugodi), and between Mysore Road and Challaghatta, according to a release.

Normal train operations on the Purple Line resumed from 1.58 p.m., around 27 minutes after the incident. BMRCL clarified that services on the Green Line and Yellow Line remained unaffected throughout the incident.

articles.title: Chola-era Leiden Copper Plates may return to Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a reply to a letter by MP Su. Venkatesan, the Union Minister of Culture confirms that repatriated antiquities are returned to their respective places of origin after verification of the provenance record

Going by a letter sent by the Union Minister of Culture to a Member of Parliament from Tamil Nadu, it appears that the historically significant Chola-era Leiden Copper Plates, brought back to India from the Netherlands, are likely to return to Tamil Nadu.

Considered a crucial historical record of the Chola period, the Anaimangalam copper plates were housed for a long time at the Leiden University in the Netherlands. These copper plates were handed over to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on May 16 in The Hague.

Madurai MP Su. Venkatesan wrote a letter to Union Minister of Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat requesting that the plates be returned to Tamil Nadu. He stated: “The copper plates originated in Nagapattinam. While every Indian can rightfully take pride in their return, heritage acquires its fullest meaning when it remains connected to its historical geography. The story recorded on these plates is inseparable from the delta, ports, temples, monasteries, and settlements of the Tamil region. To view them in Tamil Nadu is to encounter not an isolated artefact but an entire historical world. I therefore urge the government of India to ensure that the Leiden Copper Plates are permanently displayed in an appropriate institution in Tamil Nadu chosen in consultation with historians, archaeologists, cultural experts, and the State government.”

Replying to the letter, Mr. Shekhawat said the repatriated antiquities were sent back to their respective States. “The antiquities repatriated to India are generally returned to their respective places of origin after verification of the provenance record and in accordance with the established procedure,” he wrote.

Speaking to The Hindu regarding this, Mr. Venkatesan said: “I had written to the Prime Minister as well on this matter. In the past, certain antiquities repatriated to the country have been sent back to the respective States. It brings great joy that the Minister has now confirmed this through a letter.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to The Hindu regarding this, Mr. Venkatesan said: “I had written to the Prime Minister as well on this matter. articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

articles.title: U.S. President Donald Trump nominates Natalie Baker as next Ambassador to Pakistan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Ms. Baker is currently serving as charge d’affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad. She assumed the role in January 2025, following the departure of then-ambassador Donald Armin Blome

U.S. President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker to be the next U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan , paving the way for the appointment of a permanent envoy to Islamabad after a gap of nearly two years, it emerged on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
Ms. Baker is currently serving as charge d’affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad. She assumed the role in January 2025, following the departure of then-ambassador Donald Armin Blome.

The White House, in a statement, said the nomination has been submitted to the U.S. Senate, whose foreign relations committee will review it. If approved by the committee, the nomination will proceed to a vote by the full Senate. Ms. Baker would be appointed as the U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan following the Senate’s confirmation.

Earlier, she had arrived in Islamabad as Deputy Chief of Mission in August 2024, according to details available on the embassy’s website. Prior to that, she served as the Deputy Chief of Mission at the U.S. Embassy in Doha from August 2021 to July 2024.

Ms. Baker was also deployed as the Deputy Chief of Mission and charge d’affaires of the U.S. Mission to Libya, deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office at the U.S. consulate in Dubai and economic counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Kuwait.

She also served as the director of the Office of North African Affairs in the U.S. State Department’s Near Eastern Affairs Bureau. Ms. Baker is quite active in Islamabad and frequently interacts with local officials and the political leadership of Pakistan. She also oversaw the marked improvement in ties between Pakistan and the U.S. during the tenure of President Trump.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. court allows Pannun to serve NSA Doval and former intelligence chief Goyal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Order issued after U.S. State Department serves notice to officials at Indian Embassy in Washington; MEA rejects charges as ‘frivolous’, calls Pannun’s case ‘fabricated and malicious’

A U.S. court on Monday (November 9, 2026) allowed Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to serve his civil plea on National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval and former R&AW chief Samant Goel through Indian judicial channels, after the State Department submitted that it had served the notice for the two officials at the Indian Embassy in Washington.
The Ministry of External Affairs rejected the move, saying such judicial documents must be sent to the Ministry of Law and Justice in India. It called the lawsuit “frivolous”.

The lawsuit filed by Mr. Pannun, wanted in India on terror charges, is separate but linked to the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) findings of an assassination plot against him in June 2023. An undercover Drug Enforcement Agency informant had pointed to Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, and to conversations with senior Indian intelligence officials, including Vikash Yadav, regarding a conspiracy to hire a hitman to kill Mr. Pannun in New York.

Mr. Gupta pleaded guilty to the charges, and the U.S. courts have scheduled the sentencing for November 20. Mr. Yadav was arrested in Delhi in December 2023 on separate charges by Indian authorities and was given bail in April 2024.

The FBI and Canadian officials, who are investigating a similar case involving the killing of separatist Harjeet Singh Nijjar in Vancouver in June 2023, appear to have dropped earlier claims of the involvement of more senior officials, including Mr. Doval, Mr. Goel and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. However, Mr. Pannun sought to pursue his case further and filed several petitions demanding that the court summon Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel. In February 2025, when Mr. Doval accompanied Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Washington for a bilateral visit and meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump, Mr. Pannun had tried to serve the NSA with a notice and failed.

The Ministry of External Affairs indicated on Tuesday (November 10) that it was unconcerned by the latest development in the case and that the procedure for issuing the notice would require engaging the Law Ministry directly, not via the Embassy or the MEA.

“We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials, as also we reject the frivolous lawsuits. Request for serving of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India’s designated central authority, that is the Ministry of Law and Justice,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to questions at a regular briefing.

Granting permission for the summons on Monday (November 9), U.S. District Judge Katherine Polk Failla directed Mr. Pannun to prepare documents on or before November 30, including the summons addressed to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel, details of Indian law and procedure, and the route by which the summons would be issued, as well as records of previous attempts at serving the two officials under the Hague Convention.

The certificate of submission delivered to the Indian Embassy by the State Department was signed by an official and dated October 9, 2026. The State Department said in a footnote that the delivery did not mean it was taking a “position” on the case and it was a “legal obligation.

articles.title: Malaysian court clears final hurdle for former PM Najib Razak's transfer to house arrest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “A High Court in Malaysia on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) cleared all legal hurdles for the transfer of imprisoned former Prime Minister Najib Razak to his home to serve the remainder of his graft sentence under house arrest,” his lawyer said.
Najib has been behind bars since August 2022, when the Kuala Lumpur High Court upheld his graft conviction linked to a multibillion-dollar looting of the state investment fund 1MDB.
In September, Najib was granted royal clemency, allowing him to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest once he pays a court-imposed fine.

Last Friday, he left prison after his political party paid the 50 million ringgit ($12.3 million) fine but he was brought back hours later after the attorney general blocked the transfer, seeking legal clarifications.

The attorney general's request sparked a public rebuke from the palace, which said that King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar's prerogative of pardon for Najib that allowed the house arrest was clear and must be respected. It said any attempts to challenge it would amount to defying the royal order.

Najib's lawyer Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said on Tuesday all was settled for the former Prime Minister's transfer to house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur home, where he is to remain until Aug 23, 2028. Najib appeared in court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026); the transfer was expected to take place later in the day. Police later sealed off the road leading to his home. “It's a final relief, you know, great sigh to him because he has been waiting for this,” the lawyer said.

The house arrest covers only Najib's reduced, six-year sentence in his first trial for graft and not a separate, 15-year sentence handed down last December for corruption and money laundering. That sentence followed a second major trial tied to the 1MDB scandal.
Najib is also appealing that sentence, which he is to serve after the end of his first sentence. If his appeal fails, he could return to prison after his house arrest ends.

Najib, who served as Prime Minister from 2009 to 2018, has denied any wrongdoing. He is Malaysia's first former leader to be imprisoned under a sentence related to the 1MDB scandal. It marked one of the world's largest financial scandals, rippling across global markets and triggering investigations in the United States and other countries.

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 10 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Malaysian court clears final hurdle for former PM Najib Razak's transfer to house arrest

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

“A High Court in Malaysia on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) cleared all legal hurdles for the transfer of imprisoned former Prime Minister Najib Razak to his home to serve the remainder of his graft sentence under house arrest,” his lawyer said.

Najib has been behind bars since August 2022, when the Kuala Lumpur High Court upheld his graft conviction linked to a multibillion-dollar looting of the state investment fund 1MDB.

In September, Najib was granted royal clemency, allowing him to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest once he pays a court-imposed fine.

Last Friday, he left prison after his political party paid the 50 million ringgit ($12.3 million) fine but he was brought back hours later after the attorney general blocked the transfer, seeking legal clarifications.

The attorney general's request sparked a public rebuke from the palace, which said that King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar's prerogative of pardon for Najib that allowed the house arrest was clear and must be respected. It said any attempts to challenge it would amount to defying the royal order.

Najib's lawyer Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said on Tuesday all was settled for the former Prime Minister's transfer to house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur home, where he is to remain until Aug 23, 2028. Najib appeared in court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026); the transfer was expected to take place later in the day. Police later sealed off the road leading to his home. “It's a final relief, you know, great sigh to him because he has been waiting for this,” the lawyer said.

The house arrest covers only Najib's reduced, six-year sentence in his first trial for graft and not a separate, 15-year sentence handed down last December for corruption and money laundering. That sentence followed a second major trial tied to the 1MDB scandal.

Najib is also appealing that sentence, which he is to serve after the end of his first sentence. If his appeal fails, he could return to prison after his house arrest ends.

Najib, who served as Prime Minister from 2009 to 2018, has denied any wrongdoing. He is Malaysia's first former leader to be imprisoned under a sentence related to the 1MDB scandal. It marked one of the world's largest financial scandals, rippling across global markets and triggering investigations in the United States and other countries.

articles.title: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Hasina will be executed if she returns
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,’ Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.
The Bangladeshi prosecutor who secured the death sentence against ousted leader Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) she will be executed if she returns home.

Ms. Hasina, whose 15-year rule was ended by a mass uprising she tried to crush, has vowed to return in December to Bangladesh, where she was convicted of crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters.
"Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict," Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.
He added that the 79-year-old fugitive had missed the deadline to appeal against her conviction, leaving her with no further legal recourse.
"The statutory appeal period has expired, and no appeal can now be filed," he said.

The daughter of a revolutionary who led Bangladesh to independence in 1971, Ms. Hasina presided over breakneck economic growth, helping transform the South Asian nation of 170 million people from a largely agricultural economy into a global manufacturing hub.
Critics have accused Ms. Hasina of jailing political rivals, enacting harsh anti-press laws and overseeing widespread human rights abuses, including the killing of opposition activists.
Her 2024 crackdown left up to 1,400 people dead, according to the United Nations.
She fled to neighbouring India by helicopter in August 2024 as angry crowds stormed her palace.
She has remained there ever since, hidden from public view. Only occasionally has she addressed news conferences by telephone, her voice sounding frail.

articles.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The court says Delhi and the NCR bear the ‘cumulative burden of vehicular traffic’ and seeks to know what has been done to regulate in the capital the entry and plying of vehicles from neighbouring States

Forty-eight hours before Deepavali, amidst the rising crescendo of crackers heralding the festivities, a Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the people, and not the judiciary, must strike a blow against air pollution in the national capital.

Instead, the court went beyond Deepavali to highlight a consistent danger that sustains and would worsen the toxic air: vehicular emissions. On November 6, the court detected a sharp increase in issues attributable to vehicular emissions.

It told the authorities that the thick smog, which later raised the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) to almost the ‘severe’ category following Deepavali, had nowhere to go in the landlocked capital. The substantial commercial and non-commercial traffic entering Delhi would only compound the problem in the coming days.

“It must be borne in mind that Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), by virtue of their geographical and economic interconnectedness, bear the cumulative burden of vehicular traffic originating not merely within their own boundaries but also from the neighbouring States of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan,” the Supreme Court reminded the authorities in its latest order.

The issue warranted urgent and immediate intervention, the court said, directing the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), the Delhi government, the Delhi Police (Traffic department), as well as the neighbouring States of Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh to file their responses on what they have done to regulate in the national capital the entry and plying of commercial and non-commercial vehicles.

The court wanted to know about measures to regulate traffic originating from outside the national capital. These include steps taken to identify, monitor, and regulate vehicles that do not conform to prescribed emission standards, and measures to prevent the entry and operation of overage, end-of-life, or non-compliant vehicles.

The Bench has specifically sought information on the measures undertaken against violations, including the number of vehicles inspected, challaned, denied entry, and the coordination mechanisms between the authorities of Delhi and the neighbouring States for regulating inter-State vehicular movement.

The court has asked if the authorities have any “further short-term and long-term measures proposed or contemplated to mitigate vehicular emissions and reduce their contribution to the deteriorating air quality in Delhi and the National Capital Region”.

Incidentally, two separate orders of the Supreme Court passed several months ago, on January 21 and February 23 this year, had contained detailed long-term and short-term measures recommended by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to mitigate air pollution, especially caused by vehicular emissions, in Delhi.

The January 21 order had listed various CAQM recommendations, including phasing out polluting vehicles from Delhi-NCR, fortifying the pollution-under-check regime, augmentation of rail transport and metro models, revised electric vehicle policy, among others.

These include steps taken to identify, monitor, and regulate vehicles that do not conform to prescribed emission standards, and measures to prevent the entry and operation of overage, end-of-life, or non-compliant vehicles.

The Bench has specifically sought information on the measures undertaken against violations, including the number of vehicles inspected, challaned, denied entry, and the coordination mechanisms between the authorities of Delhi and the neighbouring States for regulating inter-State vehicular movement.

The court has asked if the authorities have any “further short-term and long-term measures proposed or contemplated to mitigate vehicular emissions and reduce their contribution to the deteriorating air quality in Delhi and the National Capital Region”.

Incidentally, two separate orders of the Supreme Court passed several months ago, on January 21 and February 23 this year, had contained detailed long-term and short-term measures recommended by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to mitigate air pollution, especially caused by vehicular emissions, in Delhi.

The January 21 order had listed various CAQM recommendations, including phasing out polluting vehicles from Delhi-NCR, fortifying the pollution-under-check regime, augmentation of rail transport and metro models, revised electric vehicle policy, among others.

articles.title: Cyclone-hit villages in Prakasam district remain without electricity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The villagers are going to the nearest urban centre to charge their mobile phones at a cost of ₹10 per charge and are facing difficulties in meeting their daily needs, including access to drinking water and arranging fuel for generators, sources say

Since Cyclone Murasu hit the coastline of Andhra Pradesh, several villages in Nagulappalapadu, Kanigiri, Kothapatnam, Singarayakonda, and Addanki mandals of Prakasam district have been facing continuous power outages.

Though the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited (APCPDCL) staff are undertaking restoration works on war-footing basis, the residents in these coastal villages are spending their nights by using oil lamps and candles.

According to source, the villagers are going to the nearest urban centre to charge their mobile phones at a cost of ₹10 per charge. They are facing difficulties in meeting their daily needs, including access to drinking water and arranging fuel for generators.

For more than a week, the Electricity department personnel have been restoring the electric poles and overhead wires that were damaged by the cyclone. However, the power supply has not yet been restored, leaving many villages in darkness

Speaking to The Hindu , Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar said, “Initially, we have estimated an overall expenditure of ₹500 crore to repair the electric infrastructure damaged by the cyclone. But, the budget has now crossed ₹700 crore to restore 35,000 poles across the State.”

Speaking about the restoration works in the villages of Prakasam district, he said, the APCPDCL officials are taking swift action to resolve the issues. “The domestic power supply will be rectified in a day, and it will take three days to restore agricultural and aquaculture connections”.

APCPDCL (Projects & HRD) Director T.V.S.N. Murthy supervised the repair works on the 11 kV Ammanabrolu–Chavatapalem feeder—which had experienced a power interruption—directly at the site within the Naguluppalapadu section.

Additionally, he inspected the breakdown repair works being carried out on the 11 kV Chadalavada feeder in the same section. He instructed the officials to expedite power restoration efforts and ensure that staff work in coordination to restore electricity supply as quickly as possible.

articles.title: Woman found murdered at Cheriyar in Idukki
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 57-year-old woman living alone was found brutally murdered near her home at Cheriyar, under the Santhanpara police station limits in Idukki, on Tuesday. The deceased has been identified as Rani. According to the police, the victim had been decapitated, her head bore serious injuries, and her right forearm was completely mutilated.

fullParagraphs: Sugarcane farmers in Sangareddy district have urged industries to buy the farm produce at least at ₹5,000 per tonne, considering drop in the yield due to El Nino weather phenomena and increasing cultivation costs. Citing the prices in neighbouring States including Maharashtra, the farmers have asked them to consider expenditure on fertilizers, labour, diesel and others to come to a conclusion.

Various aspects pertaining to sugarcane cultivation and procurement were discussed at a meeting on the prices held by Sangareddy Additional Collector T.L. Sangeetha with representatives of factories, farmers organisations and others, at the Collectorate on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
The Additional Collector suggested the representatives to consider the welfare of farmers and development of industries in taking the decision in two to three days.

articles.title: NDA wrests Kadapa ZPTCs from YSRCP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a record-breaking performance in the district represented by former Chief Minister and YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, the TDP-led NDA swept most of the ZPTC and MPTC constituencies in the recent elections.

Of the sixteen ZPTC seats that went to polls, the TDP bagged 12 and its ally Jana Sena won two, leaving the other two to YSRCP. The remaining were declared as won unanimously much ahead of the elections.

TDP zonal coordinator Reddeppagari Srinivasa Reddy, Pulivendula TDP in-charge B.Tech Ravi, and government whip C. Adinarayana Reddy (Jammalamadugu BJP MLA) left no stone unturned to ensure the victory of NDA in Kadapa, which was once considered the YSRCP’s stronghold.

Pulivendula, the home constituency of Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy, gave a unique result this time, as it came both as a let-down as well as a face-saver for the YSRCP. Both the Vempalle and Vemula ZPTC seats won by the YSRCP in Kadapa district are from this constituency. However, the TDP wrested the remaining seats—Pulivendula, Simhadripuram, Thondur, and Lingala.
Veteran politician and TDP former State vice-president Putha Narasimha Reddy is a major aspirant for the Kadapa ZP chairperson’s post.

When the TDP was at its low in the district, Mr. Narasimha Reddy had contested as its candidate in Kamalapuram constituency multiple times, taking head-on against Y.S. Jagan’s maternal uncle P. Ravindranath Reddy. He has reportedly secured the support of all the constituency in-charge leaders this time.

On the other hand, having won the Jammalamadugu and Yerraguntla municipalities in his constituency, Mr. Adinarayana Reddy, who holds considerable sway in northern Kadapa, has sought the ZP chief post for his nephew C. Rajesh Reddy.

articles.title: Nine cases booked during checks at rice shops in Peddapalli district, special rice sale counters opened in Peddapalli, Khammam towns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As many as nine cases were booked for short-weighing of rice bags and other violations during surprise inspections at around 50 wholesale and retail rice shops across Peddapalli district recently.
According to official sources, the inspections were conducted to curb the sale of rice at prices above the MRP, short-weighing of rice bags and other violations.
The special drive assumes significance in the wake of complaints about soaring rice prices and alleged irregularities by some traders in various parts of the district.
Officials have instructed rice traders to prominently display boards at their outlets detailing the prices of different varieties of rice and their respective stock positions, sources added.

Meanwhile, a special sale counter was opened at Kanakadurga Traders in Peddapalli town on Tuesday under the aegis of the Civil Supplies Department to make quality rice available to consumers at government-prescribed prices for different varieties.
In Khammam, the department opened its second special sale counter at the Integrated Market in VDO’s Colony on Tuesday, according to a press release.
The first such counter was set up at the Chamber of Commerce in Gandhi Chowk.

articles.title: EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra warns 'expectations low' from COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: "If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," Wopke Hoekstra said

The European Union ’s (EU) top climate official admitted on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that expectations were "low" from the COP31 summit in Turkiye, while holding out hope for "meaningful" progress on the topic of clean electricity.

"Expectations are low — that's just a reflection of reality," European Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told a group of reporters including from AFP , arguing that electrification should be the core focus of the United Nations climate talks .
"If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," he said.

The European commissioner will travel to the Turkish resort of Antalya on Monday (November 9, 2026) for the talks which run until November 20. Mr. Hoekstra voiced hope that setting an electrification target would be "at the heart" of the summit conclusions, adding: "Of course, the cleaner that electrification is, the better it is."
ALSO WATCH COP31: Can negotiators finally deliver results? | The Hindu explains

Host nation Turkiye is inviting countries to join a voluntary "electrification" pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20% today to 35% by 2035. But the EU's call for "clean" electrification could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal.
Observers expect few major breakthroughs from COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the U.S. war with Iran and Russia's conflict in Ukraine.

The European Union ’s (EU) top climate official admitted on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that expectations were "low" from the COP31 summit in Turkiye, while holding out hope for "meaningful" progress on the topic of clean electricity.

"Expectations are low — that's just a reflection of reality," European Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told a group of reporters including from AFP , arguing that electrification should be the core focus of the United Nations climate talks .

"If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," he said.

The European commissioner will travel to the Turkish resort of Antalya on Monday (November 9, 2026) for the talks which run until November 20. Mr. Hoekstra voiced hope that setting an electrification target would be "at the heart" of the summit conclusions, adding: "Of course, the cleaner that electrification is, the better it is."

ALSO WATCH COP31: Can negotiators finally deliver results? | The Hindu explains

Host nation Turkiye is inviting countries to join a voluntary "electrification" pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20% today to 35% by 2035. But the EU's call for "clean" electrification could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal.

Observers expect few major breakthroughs from COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the U.S. war with Iran and Russia's conflict in Ukraine.

The talks are also missing a major player since U.S. President Donald Trump who pulled Washington out of the Paris climate agreement has not sent officials to the talks.

"The larger picture is that the geopolitics of the times we live in are extremely complicated," said Mr. Hoekstra, who acknowledged that a string of recent COP meetings had been "underwhelming in terms of their delivery".

"There are substantial questions to be asked on how fit for purpose this design actually still is, with its unanimity" system that does not always deliver "what is actually needed," he said.

articles.title: Iran rejects France’s ‘baseless accusations’ on cyberattack
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food
Iran on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said French accusations that it was responsible for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges last month were “baseless”.
“Iran’s Foreign Ministry categorically rejects the French government’s baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France,” the Ministry said in a statement.
It added that it “strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.
Similar incidents were then reported in at least 11 other European countries in early November.

Along with summoning Iran’s ambassador and seeking European-level sanctions, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Tuesday that Paris would “rule nothing out and will take all measures — including those we may not disclose publicly — that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks”.
Tehran meanwhile said it would “not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities”.
It added that France “is merely projecting its own governance failures” with these accusations.
“A government that cannot even manage the temperature of its own refrigerators now seeks to shift the blame onto foreign actors through these preposterous accusations,” it continued.
Also on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the European Union said it would look to provide a “swift and united response” pending discussion with member states after France’s announcement.

articles.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth calls moves to impeach him a farce that will fail
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pete Hegseth made the comment ‌at a news conference a day after U.S. Representative ‌Thomas Massie, a ‌Kentucky ⁠Republican, introduced eight articles of ⁠impeachment against him
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ​on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) called moves ‌to impeach him over abuse ​of power in the ⁠Iran war a farce that would fail.
Mr. Hegseth made the comment ‌at a news conference a day after U.S. Representative ‌Thomas Massie, a ‌Kentucky ⁠Republican, introduced eight articles of ⁠impeachment against him.
In his first Pentagon news conference since May , Mr. Hegseth said ​attempts to ‌impeach President Donald Trump had failed and added: “They will fail again.”
Referring ​to the Iran war, he said: “I stand ⁠beside every one of these operations. I was proud to ‌execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow.”
In a post on X, Mr. Massie said the House would hold a first vote on ‌Tuesday on a procedural motion ​to kill the resolution.
“If we can overcome that ⁠effort, we will proceed to ⁠a real debate and vote on the Articles of ‌Impeachment,” he said.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh weighs making father’s name optional in official documents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: State consultation calls for a child-friendly policy to ensure that children of single parents, sex workers, divorced couples and orphans are not denied education, identity documents or welfare benefits

Officials of various government departments, child rights organisations, the AP Mahila Commission and NGOs on Tuesday discussed the proposal to make a father’s name optional in all official documents.

The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (APSCPCR), in association with NGOs Children India Foundation (CIF) and HELP, organised a State-level consultation on ‘Making Father’s Name Not Mandatory in Documents’ here.

APSCPCR Chairman Vetukuri A.V.S.S.N. Raju said the Commission welcomed the views of experts from various sectors on making a father’s name optional, particularly for children of sex workers, divorced couples and orphans, as well as those who did not wish to mention their fathers’ names in applications.
A.P. Mahila Commission Chairperson Rayapati Sailaja said children should not be forced to discontinue their education or be denied employment opportunities because of certain rules.

Representatives of the Education, Women Development and Child Welfare, Medical and Health, Judiciary and other departments said the government should examine the possible legal implications of the proposal and frame rules in the best interests of children.

Additional Director (Social Welfare) K. Sunil Raj Kumar and Joint Director (Women Development and Child Welfare) Vasanta Bala said their departments were not insisting on the father’s name in application forms. An official pointed out that in some cases, the requirement had become an obstacle to children’s education.

APSCPCR members P. Naga Manasa, Padmalatha, Challa Madhusudhan Rao and V. Gandhi Babu said the recommendations emerging from the consultation would be submitted to the government to ensure justice for children in need.

Joint Director (Education) V.S. Subba Rao, CIF Executive Director Hemanth Kumar, HELP Director N.V.S. Rammohan, District Legal Services Authority Secretary M.K. Vijaya Lakshmi and APSCPCR Secretary G. Uma Devi were among those who attended.

1. Core Context & Background: State consultation calls for a child-friendly policy to ensure that children of single parents, sex workers, divorced couples and orphans are not denied education, identity documents or welfare benefits

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Officials of various government departments, child rights organisations, the AP Mahila Commission and NGOs on Tuesday discussed the proposal to make a father’s name optional in all official documents.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Joint Director (Education) V.S. Subba Rao, CIF Executive Director Hemanth Kumar, HELP Director N.V.S. Rammohan, District Legal Services Authority Secretary M.K. Vijaya Lakshmi and APSCPCR Secretary G. Uma Devi were among those who attended.

articles.title: TDP-led NDA dominates Tirupati district in ZPTC/MPTC elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) led by the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has shown a clear edge over the rival YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) in the recently-held elections to MPTC/ZPTC local bodies.

Of the 35 Zilla Parishat Territorial Constituencies (ZPTC), the TDP won 25—21 in the elections and four unanimously. Similarly, its alliance partners Jana Sena and BJP won one and two seats respectively. On the other hand, the YSRCP won six seats and an independent candidate won one.

In the Mandal Parishat Territorial Constituencies (MPTC) elections, the TDP won 185 in the elections and 125 unanimously, taking its total to 310. The Jana Sena and BJP won 12 and eight respectively in the elections, apart from winning nine and five seats unanimously, taking the alliance total to 344.
The YSRCP won 85 in the polls and one unanimously, while the CPI-M won one and independents won thirteen seats.
However, the TDP suffered a major jolt in Chandragiri, the native Assembly constituency of Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu, with three out of the six mandals going to the YSRCP.

The prestigious Tirupati rural mandal, where the voting as well as the counting lasted much longer than the rest in the State, was won by Chevireddy Harshith Reddy, son of former MLA Chevireddy Bhaskar Reddy.

The YSRCP won, in spite of the efforts put in by TDP MLA Pulivarthi Nani and his spouse Pulivarthi Sudha, who represent the party’s women’s wing, to restrain the rival party leaders near the polling booths.

The YSRCP also won Yerravaripalem and Chinnagottigallu mandals in Chandragiri, making it the constituency that yielded maximum space to YSRCP. The other three seats won by it are Kodur, Chitvel, and Pellakur.

As the focus now shifts to Zilla Parishat Chairperson election (SC woman), all eyes are on Panabaka Chetana (39), daughter of TDP district president Panabaka Lakshmi and retired railway official Panabaka Krishnaiah, who won the Srikalahasti rural ZPTC seat unanimously.

A doctor by profession, her name came forward with the party’s general secretary Nara Lokesh according preference to young and educated candidates hailing from the marginalised sections. The other major aspirant is Satyavedu former MLA H. Hemalatha (78) from Nagalapuram ZPTC seat.

articles.title: T.N. government invites tenders for coverage of Assembly proceedings for two years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The work includes recording the entire session using a multi-camera setup, editing and other post-production work, and handing over the footage to the Assembly authorities for immediate telecast on satellite television channels

The Tamil Nadu government has invited tenders for complete coverage of Assembly proceedings for from January 2027 to December 2028. According to the tender document, the work includes recording the entire session using a multi-camera setup, editing and other post-production work, and handing over the footage to the Assembly authorities for immediate telecast on satellite television channels. The contract will cover 80 days of Assembly proceedings a year. Sign language interpretation and captions in Tamil and English, indicating the name and constituency of the Member speaking and the item of business being discussed, are also part of the post-production work. “Unless directed otherwise, the cameras shall show the Chair and the Member called to speak. Shots of the galleries, of Members who are not speaking, and of any disorder shall be taken only as the rules allow,” the tender document specified. The footage can be edited only to remove expunged portions based on the direction of Assembly authorities, adjournment breaks, and technical faults. Any other edits must be made only on the written directions of authorities, it added. The Assembly proceedings have been telecast live since the TVK-led government assumed office. The TVK promised the live telecast in its election manifesto. During the previous DMK regime, only the question hour was telecast live.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary jurisdiction, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and statutory bodies responsible for upholding public accountability.

articles.title: NMDC said to be in talks with Russia’s Rosatom over lithium investments
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030

Indian state-run miner NMDC Ltd. is in talks with Russia’s Rosatom to invest in Russian lithium projects, three people familiar with the matter said, as India steps up efforts to secure supplies of the metal for its battery and EV industries.
NMDC officials visited Russia last month for a conference and also held talks with state nuclear firm Rosatom, two of the people said.

The third person, who also confirmed that company officials had met with Rosatom, said NMDC was keen to explore lithium mining and processing opportunities in Russia and had also held discussions with other Russian companies.

All three people, who asked not to be named as the talks were confidential, said discussions between NMDC and Rosatom remain preliminary. A Rosatom spokesperson did not address Reuters queries about the meetings last month but said the Russian company was not currently engaged in talks with NMDC.

NMDC did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. NMDC said last year it was exploring acquisition opportunities for critical minerals in Africa, Australia and South America as part of its global mineral diversification strategy.
It has formed a 12-member team to carry out due diligence on potential critical mineral assets, one of the people said.

Last week, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet approved an incentive policy worth ₹28.14 billion ($297million) to boost domestic processing of lithium and nickel. India’s domestic processing capacity for critical minerals, including lithium, remains at a nascent stage, the government has said, leaving it heavily dependent on imports.
It currently meets lithium demand primarily through imports from China, Vietnam and Ecuador.

Despite possessing large lithium reserves, Russia currently has no commercial production. Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030.

The capture of the bases in the jungle along the border between Mon state and the Bago region marks the latest setback suffered by pro-democracy armed groups and ethnic militias fighting the army.
The reported capture could not be independently confirmed because the military does not allow journalists free access to the area, but the claim has not been challenged.

The military-backed government, which took office in April following controversial elections earlier this year, has stepped up activity in recent months on the ground and with airstrikes to retake areas controlled by the People's Defense Force, the armed wing of the major opposition National Unity Government, and ethnic militias that have been fighting the central government for greater autonomy for decades.
The PDF emerged after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021 and has since formed loose alliances with ethnic militias fighting the military.

A report in the state-run Myanma Alinn newspaper on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said the army captured 11 bases operating in the jungle area straddling the border between Mon and Bago during a six-day operation that began a week ago.

The captured positions included the special region command headquarters of the NUG and a battalion headquarters of the Karen National Liberation Army, the armed wing of the Karen National Union, a major Karen ethnic rebel group.
The paper published photos showing soldiers who captured the bases alongside ammunition seized during the operation.
Small arms, ammunition supplies, vehicles, drones and computers were captured after four armed engagements, the report said, adding that the military would continue security operations in the region.
The NUG and KNU did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Israeli forces shoot dead 14-year-old in West Bank: Palestinian officials
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Israeli forces shot dead a 14-year-old in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials said, with Israel saying it was responding to stone-throwing.
Moutaz Eyad Daghlas was killed in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, late on Monday (November 9, 2026), the Palestinian health ministry said.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds and took them to hospital, but that Israeli forces blocked access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.
The Israeli military, asked by AFP about the incident, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) it had acted to "thwart stone-hurling and terrorist attacks" in the area.

"The soldiers identified several terrorists who intended to hurl stones at a highway used by Israeli vehicles. This was in an area where stones have recently been hurled at Israeli vehicles," the military said.
"The soldiers responded by firing towards them in order to remove the threat."
Israeli forces have routinely opened live fire on Palestinians including minors who throw stones in the West Bank, which Israel has controlled since 1967.
The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem said Israeli forces killed at least 241 children or teenagers in the territory between the October 7, 2023 attack by Gaza-based Hamas and late June this year.

Violence has increased in recent weeks, especially in the run-up to Israel's October 27 election, before which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had sought to appeal to hardline settlers in the West Bank.
On October 23, Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed by Israeli forces, who later responded with a major operation in the flashpoint city.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.
